Sports.title: Leeds earn second win at Forest in three days in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Leeds United registered a second win at Nottingham Forest in three days as they booked their spot in the Carabao Cup third round.

Daniel Farke's side took the three Premier League points home on Saturday and earned a 2-0 victory in the League Cup thanks to goals from Dan James and James Justin.

Having not won at the City Ground since 1972 before the weekend, they have now triumphed there twice in 72 hours as the Yorkshire club enjoy a winning start to the new campaign.

It is not the start new Forest boss Oliver Glasner was looking for as things are yet to click, though additions are on the way with a £50m deal agreed for Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Neither side will have been jumping for joy at the prospect of a rematch so soon after Saturday's Premier League opener.

But Forest enjoyed some early promise as James Trafford was forced into a great save in the 10th minute when he had to fend away Ola Aina's cross-shot, which almost left him wrongfooted.

Then Justin was in the right place at the right time to stop Igor Jesus' header from going in.

Leeds came into it and should have gone in front midway through the first half when James got in down the right, but his pull-back was just behind Sean Longstaff, who shot straight at Matz Sels.

Image: James Justin scores Leeds' second goal at Forest

Both sides were going for it and Leeds defender Joe Rodon denied Chris Wood with a brilliant last-ditch tackle while Sels kept out James' low effort at the other end.

The Wales international showed the required composure five minutes after the restart.

Aina's wayward header allowed Longstaff to gallop forward and he played in James, who clipped home.

Forest almost hit straight back as Arnaud Kalimuendo's cutback was perfect for Wood, but Trafford did brilliantly to stop his effort from going into the bottom corner, before Noah Okafor sent an effort just wide as Leeds staged a rapid counter-attack.

Leeds sealed the victory with 15 minutes remaining but there was nothing pretty about it.

Lucas Nmecha tried to claim it as his bundled effort was blocked on the line by Williams, with Justin finally putting the ball into the back of the net.

The managers...

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner told Sky Sports

"This is a little bit the assessment after six weeks here, that maybe - and not just in the team, it's maybe in the club - that there's a little bit of ignoring the reality.

"Right now, we are far away from where we want to be, and what I'm really convinced in that where we will be.

"The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point.

"It's really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, 'Oh, Glasner is complaining'.

"No, no, no. But then maybe your best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can't deliver within six weeks.

"I'm no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.

"It doesn't make sense talking about seventh two years ago. It's hard, it's tough, but if you ignore the reality then you live in dreamland and this is never the best thing to do."

Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky Sports:

"This is what we came for, and this was my main goal.

"You play a cup run to go through. Very happy with the level of the performance, because we had to wait very long for a win here at Nottingham and to do this two times within three days at such a tough ground, this remarkable level of performance was outstanding.

"Saturday was really a tight game, but today I think it's not in doubt that it was a fully deserved win."

Sports.title: All Blacks need late surge to avoid shock defeat to Lions
Sports.content:
New Zealand fought back from an 18-point ‌deficit in the second half to beat the Lions 41-35 and avoid a shock defeat at Ellis Park on Tuesday.

It means that the All Blacks have swept all four provincial teams to remain undefeated on their six-week, eight-match tour of South Africa, on top of beating the Springboks 33-16 in ​the first Test at the weekend.

New Zealand fielded only three players from that Saturday Test victory over South Africa on the same ground and involved five injury replacements summoned on tour - including one who arrived on Monday - as well as giving a debut to prop Saula Ma'u.

Their defence struggled and missed 19 tackles over the course of the contest that saw them trail 14-0 after seven minutes.

They were still behind at half-time and 35-17 behind in the 47th minute, as the Lions threatened to become the first South African provincial side to beat New Zealand since Orange Free State, now known as the Cheetahs, in 1976.

But like the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls who the All Blacks had already beaten, the Lions are out of season and not match fit.

Having not played since May 30 in the United Rugby Championship quarter-finals, New Zealand eventually came storming back in the last 30 minutes with four successive tries.

All Blacks coach Dave Rennie thought Blackadder was phenomenal. "He's got a massive engine and was everywhere," he said.

Blackadder's Test prospects also improved after Anton Segner was ruled out of the rest of the tour.

Segner was a late withdrawal from the first Test reserves due to an ankle injury that's needed two surgeries. The injury was assessed as acute inflammatory arthritis and he won't be replaced in the squad.

Mo'unga, like New Zealand, got better as the game got older, but he and Beauden Barrett could convert only three of the team's seven tries.

On the other hand, Chris Smith, at home, converted all five of the Lions tries and hit the post with a long penalty.

Sports.title: Wilson scores on full debut as Brentford hit Birmingham for six
Sports.content:
Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins converted two headers as Brentford routed Championship side Birmingham 6-1.

The 34-year-old Wilson, who joined on a free transfer from relegated West Ham, seized his first opportunity with a crisp finish which took a deflection off defender Dael Fry, who had a debut to forget.

Brentford's Premier League quality was evident throughout and although Blues equalised through Demarai Gray just before the half-hour they were level for just seven minutes.

Image: Callum Wilson scored six minutes into his full Brentford debut

Lax defending saw Aaron Hickey and Collins score in quick succession to effectively seal the tie before half-time, with Mikkel Damsgaard getting on the end of a counter-attack to add the fourth.

Igor Thiago's smart close-range finish sent fans streaming for the exit, missing Collins' second header.

The Bees, quarter-finalists last season, had not beaten Birmingham in six previous meetings, the last a goalless draw more than five years ago in the Championship before they went on to bigger and better things which their ambitious hosts now hope to emulate.

Birmingham's priority remains promotion so, after opening with two league draws, boss Chris Davies made six changes, including goalkeeper Ryan Allsop, Fry and Argentinian striker Luis Vazquez.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Wilson produced a composed finish to put Brentford ahead just six minutes into his first competitive start for the club.

However, the gulf to a Premier League squad was evident as Keith Andrews retained only three of the team which demolished Tottenham and saw three of his newcomers score and another, Yehor Yarmoliuk, run the midfield before he was forced off with injury.

Davies wants to meet the club's aspirations by playing their way out of the Championship but it proved their undoing before they had even had chance to get a foothold in the game as they fell foul of Brentford's high press at a short goal-kick.

Paik Seung-ho was slow to react to the loose ball and Yarmoliuk played in Wilson to fire home first-time from the edge of the area with the aid of a deflection.

But a miscontrol by Jannik Schuster saw the centre-back booked for bringing down Vazquez and from Paik's short free-kick Gray drilled a deflected shot through a crowd of players.

It was a brief moment of joy in an otherwise chastening night as a failure to deal with Vitaly Janelt's chip and Wilson's strength allowed Hickey to fire home an angled shot.

Collins jumped in front of Fry to nod in a simple header from Jaidon Anthony's cross but a ruthless Brentford went for the kill and, after bringing on the likes of Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Mamadou Sangare, scored three more after the break.

The managers...

Birmingham's Chris Davies:

"My message to supporters tonight is 'sorry'. It's not very pleasant and I can understand how frustrating it is for them.

"It was a very tough evening for us, a painful evening, and incredibly disappointing to lose a game 6-1 at home.

"There were many situations where we were just not good enough to compete and I take ultimate responsibility for it - and the players will have to do it in their own minds.

"We were beaten by a team a long way ahead of us in every aspect. Was 6-1 a fair reflection? Probably."

Brentford's Keith Andrews:

"I didn't really blink an eyelid making so many changes.

"There is a huge narrative around cup games with coaches making changes but with the squad we have, there are fine margins between who plays and doesn't play.

"We needed to compete really hard to play the game we wanted. I thought overall we produced a really good performance."

Sports.title: Celtic throw away four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of Champions League against Lask
Sports.content:
Celtic threw away a four-goal lead in Austria as they missed out on the Champions League for the second year running. The Scottish champions looked to be cruising into the league stage when Callum McGregor put them 4-0 up on aggregate against Lask with a 21st-minute deflected strike.

However, they went on to endure one of their all-time European lows with a 5-1 defeat in Linz delivering a £20m-plus blow.

The Hoops had other chances in the first half but the Austrians gave themselves a lifeline when Moses Usor pounced on a loose pass from Benjamin Nygren to level on the night in the 32nd minute.

The tie began to spiral out of Celtic’s control early in the second half as Robert Ljubicic and Samuel Adeniran netted from outside the box. Martin O’Neill’s side looked like they would cling on but Florian Flecker nodded home from close range in stoppage-time to spark an additional 30 minutes.

Celtic had disappeared as an attacking force at half-time and Adeniran delivered the knockout blow that sends them into the Europa League.

The Hoops exited on penalties at the playoff stage last season after failing to sign a proven striker before drawing a blank against Kairat Almaty. Fans will this year question the decision to sell Arne Engels just ahead of the first leg after they lost control in midfield in Austria.

The quality of Celtic’s finishing had been the difference in Glasgow but Lask created chances throughout and the second leg started in similar fashion.

Celtic looked to extend their lead. Mika Baur stabbed an early chance just wide and Kasper Høgh forced a couple of first-half saves from decent opportunities. McGregor opened the scoring in between those chances when he drilled a first-time shot in off a defender after Yang Hyun-jun had played a one-two with Kieran Tierney.

The home side had exerted some pressure just before McGregor’s goal and they levelled following careless play from Nygren. The Austrian champions pulled a goal back three minutes after the restart when Usor outmuscled Auston Trusty and worked the ball inside for Ljubicic to drive home from 20 yards.

View image in fullscreen Dismayed Celtic players react to their capitulation against Lask. Photograph: Severin Aichbauer/SPP/Shutterstock

Celtic endured some nervy moments before they conceded again in the 58th minute when Adeniran curled a wonderful first-time strike into the top corner from 25 yards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Celtic were on the ropes. Several shots flew past Viljami Sinisalo’s goal before the Finn pulled off a great stop from Sascha Horvath. João Victor Tornich headed inches wide from the resulting corner.

Adeniran fired off the underside of the bar and Celtic defended with four centre-backs as Liam Scales and Dane Murray came on to join Trusty and Cameron Carter-Vickers.

With Luke McCowan, Reo Hatate and Sebastian Tounekti also off the bench, Carter-Vickers had to struggle on with cramp and Celtic could not hold out. Sinisalo made a great stop from a Tornich header but Flecker converted the rebound.

Anthony Ralston replaced Carter-Vickers as extra-time allowed O’Neill to make a further change and Celtic appeared to stem the tide. However, Adeniran fired home from 25 yards with five minutes left after dispossessing McCowan and Celtic could not threaten after Sinisalo’s penalty save denied the striker his hat-trick.

Sports.title: De Zerbi hopes Sávio’s fresh start will help Spurs’ much-needed rebrand
Sports.content:
What’s in a name? Quite a bit, judging by the discussion at Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham press conference on Tuesday, shortly after the club had completed the £75m signing of Savinho from Manchester City and the Brazil winger had let everybody know that he wanted to be called Sávio from now on. He will have that name on his Spurs shirt above his No 17, which he has taken over from Cristian Romero, the former captain who has moved to Atlético Madrid.

The 22-year-old went by Sávio at various times before his two seasons at City but there was nonetheless speculation about the reasons for the reversion. Savinho translates roughly from the Portuguese as “little Sávio”. Was it him saying that he was now an older and more mature player?

On the subject of theories, there is one about the fee, which could rise to £85m in add-ons. Even at £75m, it represents a record sale for City, who paid £30.8m to take Sávio from Troyes. Spurs are pushing to sign another attacker from City – Omar Marmoush, whose previous club Eintracht Frankfurt have a sell-on clause. Are Spurs paying more for Sávio in order to pay potentially less to City for Marmoush, which could reduce the liabilities to Eintracht?

De Zerbi has plenty on his plate after Spurs’ dismal 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday in their Premier League opener and before the Carabao Cup tie at home against Charlton on Wednesday night.

“Listen, I lost 3-0 in the first game in the Premier League … do you think for me it’s a problem if Savinho becomes Sávio?” he said, turning to face his interpreter. “If Enrico [the interpreter] becomes Savinho, it’s a problem. If Savinho stays Sávio, nothing changes for me.”

De Zerbi said the talks for Sávio had started three days after the end of last season. It has been a mini‑epic to get the deal over the line but well worth it, according to the Spurs manager, who rates Sávio as one of the best in the world for being able to get past his marker when one‑against‑one. The challenge for Sávio will be to improve his end product, particularly in terms of goals. He scored only seven for City in all competitions and only two in 53 Premier League appearances. Sávio is available for selection against Charlton, his paperwork having been completed in time.

De Zerbi did get around to accepting that Sávio’s rebrand was part of a fresh start for the player. What is not in doubt is Spurs’ need for one after Brentford, when all the excitement around a summer of heavy spending turned to frustration; a very familiar sinking feeling.

View image in fullscreen New Tottenham signings Jan Paul van Hecke (left) and Sandro Tonali (right) after Spurs conceded their second goal during their 3-0 defeat at Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It is possible to explain away the shambles against Brentford, who were not only much more joined-up but appeared to want it more in the duels. De Zerbi has attempted to do so in that way beloved of managers, emphasising he is not making excuses, you understand, just stating facts.

He had a completely new back four compared with his preferred unit from the end of last season; a new midfield pair, too. Up front from right to left, Mikey Moore, Richarlison and Mathys Tel were nobody’s idea of a trio to drive the push for Champions League football. De Zerbi was missing a host of players because of fitness issues, including Pedro Porro, Micky van de Ven, Mateus Fernandes and Dominic Solanke. Some of the issues can be traced to the slog of a pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia, which De Zerbi continues to reference in irritated tones.

These facts do not really wash. The performance against Brentford was unacceptable. There is the sense that it will work out for Spurs, mainly because they have De Zerbi and a collection of Premier League‑ready new signings. They have certainly put themselves under pressure for the visit of Charlton. A relevant statistic: Spurs have won one domestic home game in 2026 – against Everton on the final day of last season which enabled them to avoid relegation.

De Zerbi made the point that he and the squad had “started the project right now, not last season”. Which was when he was parachuted in with seven games to go; he picked up 11 points to dodge the unthinkable. “Last season, we fought to stay up,” he said. The inference was that it would take rather more to become a proper team.

On the other hand, the experiences of the previous campaign do offer reassurance. “Maybe last season was a tougher challenge to stay up than this season,” De Zerbi said. “I said to the players: last season, in a worse situation, we showed character, we showed balls. We showed pride and quality. Now we have to stay calm and to analyse better the situation – not to have an emotional reaction. We have to be intelligent.”

What De Zerbi craves is consistency, which he defined as being five wins in a row. It seems a distant goal after Brentford but De Zerbi has faith. What it will take is a change to the collective mentality. “We have to get used to winning games and games and games – we have to change habits from the last two seasons,” he said.

“For me, the Carabao Cup is like the Premier League. We are not in the condition to make differences [between the competitions]. We have to play well and get used to winning – and winning matches, not a match. We have to change the mood. And we can.”

De Zerbi said that Porro and Van de Ven will return as substitutes against Charlton and Solanke may start. James Maddison is out for two weeks with a shoulder injury suffered against Brentford. De Zerbi has a decision to make on Sávio. Victory is non-negotiable.

Sports.title: Victor Torp seals Coventry’s Carabao Cup win at Plymouth in six-goal thriller
Sports.content:
A midweek jaunt to Devon always had the makings of a tricky trip for a Coventry team focused on Premier League survival. Such feelings quickly evaporated when Frank Lampard’s side raced into a two-goal lead with just four minutes and six seconds on the clock, Taiwo Awoniyi opening his account for his new club before Jack Rudoni doubled Coventry’s advantage. But, ultimately, Coventry were made to toil before chalking up a welcome first victory of the season.

Plymouth have form for a cup upset and another was brewing when Xavier Amaechi pulled Tom Cleverley’s side level nine minutes into the second half. Coventry, to their credit, roused once more, the substitute Ephron Mason-Clark regaining the lead before Victor Torp sealed progress to the Carabao Cup third round from the penalty spot. “You’ve got to enjoy a win, always,” Lampard said. “A win is a big deal because it’s a nice feeling to take back on the bus for four hours.”

The 2,244 Coventry supporters, many of whom made the 444-mile round trip, cycled through the catalogue of songs after crisp finishes by Awoniyi and Rudoni. Then Lampard obliged when they craved a wave from a manager who led them back to the top flight after 25 years away. But the game did not turn into the non-event most would have envisaged. “It’s very easy to go: ‘Why don’t you just go 2-0 up and then beat Plymouth 5-0, 6-0?’” Lampard said. “I’ve played in these games many times with different teams and they can become awkward, especially when the flow of the game goes against you: the crowd turns, emotions catch up and all of a sudden the game feels very different. I thought we dealt OK with that, in the end.”

Plymouth were suddenly liberated at 2-0 down. The Danish centre-back Mathias Ross sent a header wide from a free-kick and a couple of minutes later Oliver Irow read Harvey White’s flighted pass and the Tottenham loanee, 24 hours after signing, drove inside Joel Latibeaudiere and drilled past the Coventry goalkeeper Dan Bentley, another debutant. From there, aside from Awoniyi heading wide unmarked, Coventry had to withstand Plymouth pressure. After fumbling White’s shot from distance, Bentley diverted Will Evans’s rebound on to his left post.

Cleverley knew the value of recording an upset, Lampard the damage of defeat. It must have crossed his mind when Amaechi levelled on 54 minutes. Amaechi swarmed Liam Kitching and pinched the ball after the Coventry defender got in a tangle and fired in. Plymouth introduced the homegrown academy graduates Tegan Finn and Caleb Roberts, joining the 17-year-old full-back Joe Mwaro, this his full debut, on the pitch. “I couldn’t be happier with the reaction and the quality we showed to make sure it was still a competitive game,” Cleverley said.

View image in fullscreen Jack Rudoni doubles Coventry’s lead from close range in the fifth minute. Photograph: Dan Mullan/Getty Images

Mason-Clark arrived for his first appearance of the season after a hamstring issue and added the fifth goal of an entertaining game. It was a galling goal from a Plymouth perspective. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s cross from the right caused problems, Mason-Clark at first failing to divert the ball goalwards. But Torp was alert to the ball dropping at the back post and squared to provide Mason-Clark the simplest of finishes, the forward poking in from inside the six-yard box.

Lampard made a triple sub, Sidiki Cherif replacing Awoniyi for his debut, while Josh Eccles and Brandon Thomas-Asante also entered. Joe Edwards, the Plymouth midfielder, arrived from the bench but his first notable action was to inadvertently swipe at Thomas-Asante in the box when trying to clear the leftovers of a Coventry corner, giving the referee, Elliott Swallow, no choice but to award a penalty. Torp capped the scoring, thrashing the spot-kick into the top corner.

For Cleverley, this also represented a touchline duel with a friend and a former England teammate and he had spoken on the eve of the game of wanting English coaches like Lampard and Michael Carrick, another former teammate, to succeed. “If you do well in it, you’re great for a moment, if you don’t do so well, then you’re not,” Lampard said after. “If you have the English tag, I do think we’ve got a bit of a bracket of saying: ‘There’s another one [struggling].’ Hopefully we’re not idiots and we can show that over a period of time and do our jobs well.”

Sports.title: Carabao Cup roundup: Leeds beat Forest again, Brentford hit Birmingham for six
Sports.content:
Leeds secured a second win at Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest in three days to book a spot in the Carabao Cup third round. Dan James’s 50th-minute opener and a Neco Williams own goal earned a 2-0 victory for Daniel Farke’s side to back up Saturday’s 1-0 league success.

Before the weekend, the West Yorkshire club had not won at the City Ground since 1972. After defeat, new Forest manager Oliver Glasner said he is not a “magician”.

“Right now, we are far away from where we want to be,” Glasner said. “The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point.

“It’s really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, ‘Oh, Glasner is complaining’. No, no, no. But then maybe your best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can’t deliver within six weeks. I’m no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.”

Callum Wilson scored just six minutes into his full debut and captain Nathan Collins headed home twice as Brentford hammered Birmingham 6-1 at St Andrew’s. Aaron Hickey, Mikkel Damsgaard and Igor Thiago were also on target for the Bees after Demarai Gray briefly cancelled out Wilson’s opener.

League One Peterborough stormed into round three by thumping Championship Watford 5-1 at Vicarage Road. Hornets head coach Alessio Dionisi paid a heavy price for making 11 changes as James Clarridge’s own goal, Harry Leonard’s double and strikes from Bolu Shofowoke and Harrison Jones clinched an emphatic upset.

Hull required penalties to beat second-tier Stoke. The Tigers won 5-4 in the shootout after Kieran Dowell cancelled out Robert Bozenik’s goal in a 1-1 draw.

Teenager Josh Ayala scored twice on his full professional debut as West Ham came from behind to thrash Championship rivals Southampton 4-1. Taty Castellanos and Jarrod Bowen sealed the Hammers’ victory at St Mary’s after 19-year-old Ayala’s double overturned Léo Scienza’s opener.

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo saluted Ajala afterwards. “It is important for Josh,” he said. “He works hard every day in training to get chances in games. We are delighted he took the opportunity.”

Marcelino Núñez scored a sensational goal from the halfway line as part of a brace to help Ipswich beat Leicester 3-1.

Middlesbrough avenged last season’s exit at the hands of Doncaster with a 3-1 win thanks to goals from Kyle Joseph, Will Lankshear and Jeremy Sarmiento.

Norwich forward Ante Crnac marked his first appearance in 10 months after a serious knee injury by scoring the winner in a 2-1 victory at Cardiff.

Saheed Olagunju’s debut goal helped Wolves beat Sheffield Wednesday 2-0 at Hillsborough, while Ched Evans scored twice as Fleetwood thrashed League Two rivals Shrewsbury 4-0.

Romelle Donovan’s first Sheffield United goal secured a 2-1 victory at fellow Championship side Blackburn. Leyton Orient won 6-5 on penalties away to Walsall after a goalless draw.

Elsewhere, Lincoln were 4-1 victors at Blackpool, Jake Cooper earned Millwall a 1-0 success at Cambridge, League One Barnsley overcame fourth-tier Crewe 3-2 at Oakwell, and Reading eased to a 3-0 win at Stevenage.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw land PFA Player of the Year awards
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned Professional Footballers’ Association Player of the Year as Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw won the women’s award for the second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcome a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick to earn a Champions League return.

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals. He said: “It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it’s probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment.”

The Portugal international is the club’s first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009-10, and adds to his Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women’s Player of the Year award for the second time. The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again having scored 21 goals on the way to a third consecutive Golden Boot and her maiden Women’s Super League title.

Arsenal’s Olivia Smith picked up the women’s PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool before continuing her form in the capital.

Manchester City’s Nico O’Reilly was named men’s PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze. The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City teammates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O’Reilly said: “I had a great season. I’m very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I’m over the moon how it turned out.”

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurriën Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford’s Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by teammates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year’s PFA Women’s Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo. Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United’s Jess Park were also included in the team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hayden Hackney, now of Everton, was named Championship PFA Players’ Player of the Year for his performances for defeated play-off finalists Middlesbrough.

Dom Ballard, who scored a jaw-dropping effort for new club Bristol City at the weekend, collected the League One award for a goal-laden season at Leyton Orient.

Swindon striker Aaron Drinan’s performances saw him collect the League Two award, while Lily Crosthwaite of Birmingham took the WSL2 player accolade.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football. Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland’s most capped performer having represented his country on 102 occasions. The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn’s Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup. Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

Sports.title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere.

Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.

Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.

Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.

West Ham’s clear out after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.

Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.

West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are plan to strengthen further.

Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out. The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.

Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts, and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Xavi hopes time at the ‘university of football’ will end with Dutch success
Sports.content:
“My feeling today is that I’m going to the university of football.” Those were Xavi Hernández’s opening words at his presentation as the Netherlands coach on Tuesday. “I learned a lot from this university of football during my career as a player and as a coach. I have many connections with this country.”

Those connections date back to when Xavi was drafted as a youngster into La Masia, the famed Barcelona academy whose fundamentals are rooted in Dutch total football, inspired by Rinus Michels and Johan Cruyff. Xavi’s first-team debut came under Louis van Gaal, and he spent many years under Frank Rijkaard before becoming one of the main pillars of the dream team under Pep Guardiola, who was hugely inspired by Cruyff.

Xavi opened a Cruyff court – a multifunctional sport space for children – with Cruyff in his home town of Terrassa in 2014, and on Tuesday shared special memories of his time with Cruyff, who died in 2016. “With Johan in the last period of his life I had some meetings,” he said. “And he was always positive. Even when he was sick, he was positive. This is what I learned: always smiling. This is what I want to show here to the players. My first goal is to help them, and then enjoy the process. And we will be in a process to win.”

Xavi says he wants to “dominate the game, to take the initiative with the ball and at the same time our goal is to show everybody a team with passion, with desire and ambition. And this is very important for me as a coach.”

In the Netherlands, there has always been a strong emphasis on attacking football, which is why Xavi fitted the bill. The Catalan was asked whether he would use five defenders, as Van Gaal and Ronald Koeman did at times in recent years. “That this is not my idea,” he said. “We want to play in another system [like] 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 3-4-3. In those systems we can dominate the game more.”

Xavi said he had spoken to Frenkie de Jong – whom he coached at Barcelona – and Virgil van Dijk. He added that he would speak again to Van Dijk, the captain, in the near future to hear his ambitions with the team.

The 46-year-old was also clear he is willing to select players from the Saudi Pro League, something more relevant after Tijjani Reijnders moved from Manchester City to Al-Qadsiah last week. Two years ago, Koeman was clear when Steven Bergwijn moved to Al-Ittihad that the forward would no longer be selected because the league did not match the level he expected from his players.

View image in fullscreen Xavi Hernández said he wants to play attacking systems with the Netherlands to ‘dominate the game more’. Photograph: Stefan Koops/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

“It’s a good league as well,” Xavi said. “Maybe we choose some players from Saudi, from Eredivisie, Premier League, La Liga. I don’t care about the leagues, I care about the performances and the players.”

Nigel de Jong, the director of elite football at the Dutch football federation (KNVB), had earlier been open about the process that led to Xavi’s appointment. He said he had first tested the waters with Guardiola, who indicated he did not want to take a job in the near future, before holding two meetings with Arne Slot, who eventually chose to remain a club coach.

De Jong then invited Xavi to Amsterdam for a meeting also attended by Clarence Seedorf, a member of the KNVB’s supervisory board. The following day De Jong and Seedorf spoke at length with Michael Reiziger, the Netherlands’ under-21s coach, who played alongside Xavi at Barcelona for several years.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They were considering promoting Reiziger in a way similar to Luis de la Fuente’s journey with Spain, his knowledge of the country’s upcoming talents regarded as a major plus. When the meeting with Reiziger became known in the Dutch media, there was an assumption the former full-back would become the national team coach. But then, on 12 August, the KNVB announced Xavi, a decision that seemingly came out of the blue.

Xavi said drily that he was fine with the process. “Well, it’s not a bad position, after Guardiola and after Slot, no? At least you are at the podium. I don’t care if I’m the third [choice] or I’m the 10th. It’s a big honour to be here. He [De Jong] explained to me, very honestly: ‘We need your philosophy, we need to change with ambition, with passion.’ And we will work in this way.”

First up for Xavi is a Nations League game against Germany in Amsterdam on 24 September, when he will face Jürgen Klopp, who is also starting a new job. “I feel excited, I feel motivated,” Xavi said, “because we are playing against Germany, one of the best teams in Europe, one of the best coaches in recent years.”

Xavi, speaking in front of his staff, including Ruud van Nistelrooy, wants his team to adopt the Dutch style he saw as a young boy. “I remember when I was a kid, watching the Netherlands and watching good football,” he said, “and this is my way, this is my target.”

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling faces two years in jail after being charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling faces two years in jail after being charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after his £270,000 Lamborghini crashed in May, it has been reported.

The former Premier League star, 31, who was arrested at the scene of the collision, faces two years in prison if convicted of the charges.

Police were called to the M3 in Hampshire on May 28 to reports of a Lamborghini swerving around the road just before 9am.

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail appeared to show the black luxury 4x4 veering across the three carriageways as other vehicles dodged out of the way.

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon - which is how people ingest laughing gas, also known as 'hippy crack'.

Minutes later, Sterling allegedly crashed the vehicle into the motorway barriers and was cuffed by Hampshire Police.

The force said he would not give a sample after his arrest - leading to a third charge of failing to supply a specimen.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman told The Sun: 'Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

Raheem Sterling has reportedly been charged with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide, and failing to supply a specimen

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail showed Starling's black Lamborghini M-way scraping the motorway central reservation, minutes before it crashed

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon, just visible as a dark circle above

'The charges come following a single-vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.'

They added that Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on September 15.

The charges mark a new low for Sterling, who left Chelsea in January after being dropped from their line-up and not playing since May 2024.

In February, he joined Dutch club Feyenoord Rotterdam, but that deal ended in summer and he has been without a club since - despite wanting to play.

The motorist who provided the dashcam footage of Sterling's sports car swerving told the Mail: 'I was in the middle lane and without warning a black Lamborghini pulled in front of me, forcing me to slow.

'I dropped back. I'm a driving instructor after all.

'The car turned back into the inside lane but the driver put his foot down and veered right across all three lanes and seemed to just avoid hitting the central reservation.

'It's a powerful car and he could have easily gone through the central reservation if he'd hit the accelerator.

'A van driver behind him was forced to brake and he then shot off again and turned back across three lanes again into the inside lane.

Sterling is engaged to long-term girlfriend Paige Milian (pictured)

Sterling, here playing for Feyenoord in February, has been without a team since the summer

'This was all caught on dashcam from 8.45am on Thursday. It was just before Junction 4a southbound on the M3.

'The motorist was all over the place but I had no idea it was Raheem Sterling until I saw that he'd been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving by the Minley Interchange.

'I like Raheem but as a driving instructor I'm very concerned.

'He could have easily caused himself - and others - a great deal of harm. He was very fortunate that he did not do so.'

Sterling's representatives declined to comment when contacted by the Daily Mail after the crash, but a source close to the player explained how he had had a hellish two years.

The source said: 'The psychological strain that has been put on him is immeasurable. Isolated. The second he touches a ball, being told he's a flop and he's finished. Mocked. Heckled.

'He moved to the Netherlands to escape and rediscover his love for the game but the negativity followed. It's been an extremely tough couple of years for him and this incident encompasses that.'

Sterling started his career at QPR but broke through at Liverpool as a teenager, before leaving Anfield for Manchester City in 2015, where he won ten major trophies, including the Premier League four times.

He played 82 times for the England senior team, with his last appearance in the 2-1 defeat by France in the quarter-finals of the 2022 World Cup.

However, since leaving City for Chelsea in a £50million deal in 2022 he has endured a torrid spell, which saw him exiled at Stamford Bridge before a failed loan spell with Arsenal and a move to Dutch giants Feyenoord, where he made just eight appearances with no goals.

Sports.title: 'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup
Sports.content:
'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

A statistic currently going around about Everton being the only club among the Football League's 92 not to have won a trophy, a title or promotion, or been relegated, since the turn of the century has contributed to a pessimism which made a gathering of the club’s faithful last Friday evening very welcome.

The occasion, at the Denbigh Castle pub, a legendary gathering place for Evertonians in central Liverpool, celebrated the former Everton captain Mike Lyons, whose life and career have been charted in a fine new book.

The aching sadness underlying an occasion in which Lyons' former team-mates took turns to relate stories of the indefatigable, generous and hugely talented team-mate they knew and loved, is that the man in question is struggling now and could not be there.

His daughter Francesca, who lives near Liverpool and calls him every day at the care home in Perth, Australia, where he is living with dementia, reminds him how cherished he is among fans. Lyons, 74, knew that the event was taking place and he knows about the book, The Man Who Bled Blue, a meticulously researched and beautifully written biography by the journalist and author Simon Hart. But his brain has frayed terribly. His family and friends have helped Hart piece together the life story.

He would certainly empathise with those 21st century fans who yearn for silverware – any silverware – and not least the League Cup, which sends the team to Preston, David Moyes’ old club, on Wednesday night. Everton were reigning English champions, four days away from contesting a European Cup quarter-final, when Lyons made his debut in March 1971.

Mick Lyons made 473 appearances for Everton in his 12 years on Merseyside, scoring 59 goals

‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses’

With Everton team-mates Martin Dobson (left) and Bob Latchford (right)

Yet his 11 years as an Everton player did not yield him a single honour. Liverpool won 15 in that time. By 1982, Lyons was on his way to Sheffield Wednesday, missing by a couple of years the start of the glorious era when Everton won the FA Cup and two titles.

Had Lyons been at Friday’s event, talk would inevitably have turned to the League Cup – and his huge role in Everton's marathon against Aston Villa in the 1977 final, won by Villa in a second replay at Old Trafford. It remains one of the greatest clashes in the tournament's history and was the closest Lyons ever came to silverware with Everton.

Evertonians still remember the intensity of his celebration when he scored an equaliser in front of the Stretford End in the second replay. ‘Michael was more animated there than at any other goal he scored,’ his brother, Joe, tells Hart in the book. (To his family, Lyons has always been ‘Michael.’) Fatefully, he was then asked to push up as a utility centre-forward as Everton chased a winner – it’s a strategy still known as ‘Doing a Mike Lyons’ among Evertonians – and a hole materialised at the back which Villa exploited to score a late winner. In the seclusion of the car on the way home, Lyons wept.

This story teaches us, among other things, that barren times can produce some of the greatest heroes, like Lyons, and that the League Cup can bring such indelible memories that Everton, who have not always fielded strong teams in recent times, should see it as an opportunity.

Hart relates how, despite the initial Wembley final not yielding a winner, the team still appeared on a planned open-bus tour of Liverpool for which vast crowds turned out. The first replay, a thrilling 1-1 draw in Sheffield rescued by a late Bob Latchford goal, would remain one of Lyons’ favourite nights of his career. He later described the noise made by Evertonians that night as ‘something I’ll always treasure. It embodied everything I’ve always felt for this club’.

The biography’s title, alongside an image of Lyons with a gashed face as he leaves the pitch after Everton’s 1980 FA Cup semi-final against West Ham – another one they lost – captures his contribution. His myriad cuts, blows and collisions form a backdrop to the book. ‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses.’

The book’s beauty also resides in its small details, capturing the boundless enthusiasm and often comic innocence which accompanied Lyons huge professionalism and work ethic.

He drove a club-issue Lada with his name emblazoned down the side. He eschewed the posh Liverpool hair salon which the players attended for their curly perms in favour of the work of team-mate Roger Kenyon’s wife Jackie, a hairdresser. Mrs Kenyon and Lyons’ wife Tricia were in such deep conversation in the Lyons’ kitchen that the perm solution was left in the Everton captain’s hair for too long. It was a catastrophe.

Shaking hands with Liverpool captain Emlyn Hughes ahead of the 1977 FA Cup semi-final at Maine Road

It is now 31 years since Everton last lifted a trophy, the 1995 FA Cup

The League Cup is the only major domestic trophy that Everton have never won, and it is time they rectified that point

You could have heard a pin drop in that Liverpool pub on Friday night when Francesca Lyons told the 100 or so people gathered that her father would have been humbled by all this attention. The consequences of his repeated heading of the ball are the same that so many old pros have had to face, full on, and Francesca has been an impressive advocate for football's need to do more for them.

There is a reason why the book’s subtitle is The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons. The Villa captain in the 1977 final was Chris Nicholl, who lived with the form of dementia caused by repeatedly heading footballs during his playing career, before he passed away in 2024.

But Friday evening was about the life-affirming qualities of a captain and player who, Francesca insisted, would not have had his life any other way. ‘He has always been so upbeat and fun,’ she said. ‘He would have probably laughed off all the attention because he’s always been so humble.’

Moyes, who also loves the bones of Everton, has a deep understanding of Lyons’ contribution. He and his long-time assistant Billy McKinlay paid him a visit during an Everton pre-season tour of Australia some time back. The League Cup remains a trophy Everton have never won. Lyons, who still watches the club’s games from Perth, would smile to see them finally lift the three-handled trophy next March, 50 years on from that legendary three-game marathon against Villa.

The Man Who Bled Blue: The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons by Simon Hart is published by Mount Vernon Publishing.

Sports.title: LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply
Sports.content:
LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply

Austrians reach Champions League at Celtic's expense after 5-4 aggregate win

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Since embarking on their maiden European voyage in the old Inter-City Fairs Cup some 64 years ago, Celtic have scaled some dizzying heights and experienced some crushing lows.

Perhaps never before has the sense of sheer desolation felt quite as acute as it did when the final whistle signal sounded last night in northern Austria.

On an occasion when Martin O'Neill's side simply wilted before your eyes, a return ticket to the big stage was ripped up and the accompanying £40million in prize money slipped through the club's hands.

It was a catastrophic outcome – one which beggared belief after such a commanding display in Glasgow six days previously.

How could a side which was in such complete control of a tie at the midway point look so ramshackle and lost?

Celtic players are dejected in Austria as their Champions League bid disintegrates

It's much too easy to cite complacency on the players' part as the reason why Celtic again crashed out at this stage. They didn't initially play like a team that already believed the job was done. They just stopped playing.

Not since collapsing away to MTK Hungarian in 1963-64 had Celtic surrendered a three-goal first leg lead. The fallout from this will be nuclear.

For all the board were given some credit for lavishing £30million on four players, two of those – Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan – arrived too late in the window to take this match in their stride.

And where are the others which O'Neill evidently needed in the door sooner? The left-back, the holding midfielder that European football demands, the additional creative influence?

A club that's still in profit for this window didn't get its act together in good time. And, accordingly, it won't be returning to the big stage.

And so, the name of LASK joins that of AEK Athens, Cluj, Ferencvaros, Midtjylland, Kairat Almaty as sides to have knocked Celtic out in Champions League qualification in recent times.

You could lose one of those ties, maybe two, even if you are going about things the right way. When you chalk up six losses on the spin, you aren't behaving like a serious football club.

Few who watched this debacle unfold will ever have seen anything like it. It was scarcely believable.

When Callum McGregor found the net in 21 minutes, Celtic were four goals up on aggregate and contemplating what Thursday's draw in Monaco might bring.

While Benjamin Nygren's error allowed Moses Usor to level on the night before the break, there was no need to panic.

But that's exactly what unfolded. Auston Trusty's error played a part in Robert Ljubicic cutting the aggregate deficit to two.

Camilo Duran looks pained as Celtic suffer in Austria

More untidy defending then saw Samuel Adeniran net LASK's third and at that point Celtic were running about with their hair on fire.

With the Austrians completely dominant and managing 31 attempts in regulation time, the only wonder was that it took them until the 90th minute to square the tie with substitute Florian Flecker heading home a rebound.

Adeniran sealed an extraordinary comeback in extra-time following another elementary error and even had the luxury of having a penalty saved.

Celtic actually started the game fairly well. Baur's cross had a little too much on it for Kasper Hogh.

The German's interception sent Hogh in on goal. A poor execution ensured the keeper saved comfortably.

LASK were not shy at trying their luck from distance or shelling the box with crosses.

They were left with their heads in their hands when Xavier Mbuyamba failed to convert at the back post following a flick-on.

O'Neill's heart would have skipped a beat when Melayro Bogarde's strike took a deflection off McGregor and bounced off the upright.

Arriving just before the midway point in the first half, Celtic's opener owed everything to their pace and invention down the left flank.

Hyun-jun Yang played the ball back to Kieran Tierney and darted forward. Having taken the return ball, he bobbed and weaved while assessing his options.

LASK's Samuel Adeniran celebrates scoring his team's fifth goal against Celtic

Having correctly identified that McGregor was best placed to capitalise, he cut the ball back. The skipper's left-foot strike came off the outstretched leg of Andres Andrade and beat Lukas Jungwirth in goal.

Hogh looked like removing any lingering doubt soon after only for a nudge in his back to put him off.

With LASK looking increasingly frustrated, Adeniran pulled a shot wide of the far post then left one on Colby Donovan.

Celtic should have been coasting at half-time. Instead, LASK gave them something to worry about.

There was nothing wrong with Cameron Carter-Vickers' pass to Nygren. The Swede went blind with his attempted pass back.

Moses Usor could hardly believe his luck. A calm first-time finish gave the Austrians hope.

For O'Neill's players, it was a question of staying disciplined and sticking to their respective tasks at the outset of the second period.

Yet within three minutes, Trusty got himself done for pace and power on the left. LASK moved the ball into the central Robert Ljubicic.

The playmaker's shot from the edge of the box did fly through a thicket of legs. Still, Sinisalo was too easily beaten.

Ten minutes later, the unthinkable inched ever closer. A long punt up the park found Celtic's defence disjointed.

Donovan gave Ljubicic too much space to pick a pass to Adeniran. To that point in the tie, the American had played like his laces had been tied together. Not this time. His cushioned left-foot strike curled away from the outstretched arm of Sinisalo. Celtic were in trouble.

Reo Hatate and Seb Tounekti were introduced before Luke McCowan and Liam Scales joined them. Dane Murray later replaced the stricken Donovan.

Sinisalo did well to turn Sascha Horvath's deflected strike wide then watched Joao Viktor Tornich's point blank header flash wide.

When Adeniran's strike thumped the underside of the bar, the ball hit Sinisalo's back but stayed out. Celtic were riding their luck.

Celtic players call for offside after Florian Flecker's goal for LASK

O'Neill picked up a booking for venting his growing frustrations at the officials. Of greater concern was Kasper Jorgensen's shot which flew narrowly wide. Celtic were handing the ball as if it was a hot potato.

The clock had just struck 90 minutes when they conceded again. Finding himself in acres of space on the left, George Bello crossed. Sinisalo did brilliantly to prevent an initial header from finding the net but could do nothing as sub Florian Flecker nodded home the rebound.

All the momentum was with the Austrians in extra-time. Celtic got through the first period only to concede a fifth four minutes after the turnaround.

McCowan became the latest visiting player to make an enforced error when he won the ball on the edge of his own box and had his pocket picked. The ball was worked to Adeniran at the edge of the box who beat Sinisalo all too easily.

The Finn kept Celtic breathing by saving Adeniran's penalty after Hatate had felled Krystof Danek. It only prolonged the agony.

Sports.title: Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... United youngster linked with Feyenoord Manchester United forward Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Feyenoord. The Dutch side, coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst, want cover in case they lose a forward in the final stages of the window. Obi Martin, a Denmark U21 international, had interest from Cologne earlier in the window. Feyenoord would also offer Champions League football. Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Dutch side Feyenoord Forest close in on Delap deal Nottingham Forest and Chelsea are closing on a £45million deal for Liam Delap. Talks intensified on Monday following Chelsea's game at Fulham and a verbal agreement is in place for the 23-year-old to link up with Oliver Glasner's team. He is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours. Liam Delap is expected to undergo a Nottingham Forest medical in the next 24 hours United complete Baleba deal Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal. ‘I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level,' said the 22-year-old, who has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford. ‘The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.’ For more on this story click HERE Carlos Baleba with Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox Gonzalez says goodbye to City ahead of £50m Newcastle move Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is travelling to the North East to finalise his £50m move to Newcastle United. The 24-year-old Spaniard will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours. Gonzalez said his farewells to City team-mates this morning and the deal is set to be £47m plus £3m in add-ons. Nico Gonzalez will become Newcastle United's latest signing of the summer City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League. Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020. Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested. Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham Bees still buzzing about Diouf Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season. West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre. The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league. AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him . Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City. They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah. Forest have also opened talks with Celta Vigo for right-back Javi Rueda. Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024. Villa enquire over Kofane Aston Villa have made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for striker Christian Kofane. As well as working on Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, Villa want another forward. As Daily Mail Sport revealed, they were rebuffed in an enquiry for Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta but have now turned to Kofane. The 20-year-old's agent was in England earlier this summer talking to the likes of Everton and Arsenal. However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell. Wrexham close on £8m move Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push. Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million. Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers. Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old. Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m. They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti. NATHAN SALT Olympiacos in for Edson Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan. The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far. Doncaster living the life O'Reilly Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan. A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe. Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season Tottenham seal Savinho deal Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho. Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons. Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City. Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world. 'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.' De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity. 'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.' Sports.title: Leeds do the double over Nottingham Forest: Daniel Farke's side win at the City Ground for the second time in just FOUR days with Carabao Cup triumph - and Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for new boss Oliver Glasner
Sports.content:
Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for Nottingham Forest. Two games into Oliver Glasner’s reign at the City Ground, two defeats to Leeds United, and zero goals. He started three strikers and they still couldn’t score. And, so, for the second time in four days, Daniel Farke’s team came to town and took full advantage of a team still trying to find their new identity. First for three points on Saturday, now for a place in the League Cup third round. Daniel James was afforded the freedom of West Bridgford all evening and fittingly gave Leeds the lead before James Justin bundled in a second after a long throw caused chaos in the Forest box. Glasner’s side, once again, looked in desperate need of new blood. Thankfully, news emerged a few hours before kick-off that Forest had agreed a club-record fee of £45million, potentially rising to £50m, for the Chelsea striker. A remarkable whack for a player who scored just one Premier League goal last season and wasn’t even training with the first-team. Daniel James scored the opening goal as Leeds United won 2-0 at Nottingham Forest James Justin (right) scored the second as Leeds knocked Forest out of the Carabao Cup Delap is by no means the first budding talent to be chewed up and spat out by Chelsea and if Glasner can unleash the old-fashioned centre-forward that thrived at Ipswich, he would be just what they need. Glasner likes a physical focal point, as he had at Palace in Jean-Philippe Mateta, to hold it all together and bring team-mates around him into play as those around him attack with pace. ‘A frustrating night,’ said Glasner, who refused to comment on Delap’s impending arrival. ‘Last season told everyone what is needed, not just tonight. Nine months of relegation battle, losing maybe your top midfielder and now just six weeks together. The reality is no magician, no messiah, just hard work.’ That’s why Forest still look better when Chris Wood leading the line but he’s 35 in December and struggles with injury. He had the best chances of the night for Forest but couldn’t take any of them. A sensational last-ditch tackle from Joe Rodon denied him after a neat nutmeg of Nico Elvedi left him with just James Trafford to beat. Wood had another fine chance in the second half, too, but couldn’t beat Trafford from eight yards. Trafford is quickly starting to enjoy his football again. Two matches since his £40m move from Manchester City and two clean sheets. ‘It was a remarkable level of performance,’ said Leeds boss Farke. ‘Never in doubt, it was a fully deserved win. I saw how dominant we can be against really good sides.’ Forest boss Oliver Glasner has plenty to mull over after starting his reign with two defeats Carabao Cup R2 results: August 25 Cardiff City 1-2 Norwich City Doncaster Rovers 1-3 Middlesbrough Barnsley 3-2 Crewe Alexandra Blackburn Rovers 1-2 Sheffield United Blackpool 1-4 Lincoln City Cambridge United 0-1 Millwall Fletwood Town 4-0 Shrewsbury Town Ipswich Town 3-1 Leicester City Plymouth Argyle 2-4 Coventry City Sheffield Wednesday 0-2 Wolverhampton Wanderers Southampton 1-4 West Ham United Stevenage 0-3 Reading Stoke City 1-1 Hull City* (4-5 on penalties) Walsall 0-0 Leyton Orient* (5-6 on penalties) Watford 1-5 Peterborough Town Birmingham City 1-6 Brentford Nottingham Forest 0-2 Leeds United Forest, meanwhile, are still getting used to playing Glasner’s way and James repeatedly exploited the space behind wing-back Williams. James whipped one cross in to set up a glorious chance for Sean Longstaff, saw a shot of his own saved by Matz Sels. On 50 minutes, Williams bombed forward only for Arnaud Kalimuemdo to give the ball away and leave Forest exposed. Longstaff slipped in James who fired past Sels before Williams could get back. The puzzle of how to replace Elliot Anderson remains unsolved. Leeds’ second summed it all up as the ball bounced its way to the back post, Williams tried to clear it but couldn’t, almost put it into his own net, only for Justin and Lucas Nmecha to finally help it in. At least it was a more entertaining spectacle than four days ago. Neither side deserved to win that one. Leeds warranted every bit of their victory this time. The boos at full-time told you that.
