World.title: Haiti: UN chief condemns Haiti attack that killed 47
World.content:
The UN Secretary General has condemned a violent attack that left at least 47 dead and saw over 50 more kidnapped.

At least 47 people, including at least five children, were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped by armed men in Haiti on Sunday, the United Nations confirmed on Tuesday.

The incident, which took place in Kenscoff on the outskirts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in the troubled Caribbean country in recent years.

In a video posted on social media, a gang leader threatened to murder hostages if Haiti's National Police kill any of his men in an attempt to rescue people.

"If any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them," he said.

One resident told the Associated Press that gang members had kidnapped his brother, stepmother, stepfather and two cousins. He said his 16-year-old niece was also kidnapped and raped but managed to escape.

"I had to run over bodies," he said, recalling his own escape. "I can't sleep knowing all these people died."

Haiti: UN condemns violence

United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres condemned the attack which he said underscored the "alarming security conditions" in Haiti and amplified the need for both domestic and international security efforts.

Via a spokesman, he called for Haitian authorities to "ensure that those responsible for such attacks are held accountable," including through specialized judicial units recently established with international support to investigate mass crimes.

How the West messed with Haiti To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Strategic location targeted by gangs

Kenscoff is located around 10 kilometers south of Port-au-Prince at an altitude of around 2,000 meters.

Thanks to its cooler climate, is considered a relatively desirable residential area, while its mountainous location also makes it strategically important when it comes to control of key road connections.

Kenscoff is also close to the political institutions, embassies and banks of Pétion-Ville, a comparatively affluent suburb of the capital.

The first major attack on Kenscoff occurred in January 2025. Since then, there have been sporadic attacks in the mountains surrounding the city center.

But Sunday's attack was the largest yet, shattering the belief that security in the Caribbean country was improving.

Haiti: 'Major security test for government'

"This is a major political and security test for the government, for the police and for the international mission," said Romain Le Cour, head of the Haiti Observatory at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime.

Le Cour believes the threat of executing hostages is a trap: if the authorities don't act, they will be seen to be abandoning the captives; but if they do and more people die, the gangs will blame the state.

More than 3,050 people were reported to have been killed in Haiti between January to June, according to UN statistics released this week, while gang violence has displaced an estimated 1.5 million more.

The UN also noted that nearly 800 rapes and over 80 kidnappings were reported between April and June alone.

"These figures represent only a portion of the total number of people kidnapped," read a statement, pointing out that victims' relatives often choose to negotiate directly with the kidnappers in the belief that this approach will secure a quicker release and avoid possible reprisals.

Haitians prepare for US immigration crackdown To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

World.title: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon
World.content:
Dolly Parton was one of the world's most successful artists. On Tuesday, her family announced that she passed away at 80. Here are some important and extraordinary facts about the country music superstar.

More than 100 million records sold, 25 No. 1 hits on the US country charts, 11 Grammys and three Emmys — country star Dolly Parton was one of the most successful singers in the world. On Tuesday, her nephew Bryan Seaver announced in a video shared on Parton's social media channgels that his aunt had passed away.

"Dolly... opened doors for generations of singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent," Seaver said in the video. "She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history."

Here are eight facts from eight decades of Dolly Parton.

1. Cornmeal for the doctor

Dolly Parton came from humble beginnings, growing up with 11 siblings in Sevier County, Tennessee.

Born on January 19, 1946, her parents paid the doctor who assisted at her birth with a sack of cornmeal — though some sources claim it was oats.

Parton was born into a musical family and learned to play the guitar when she was 7. She gave her first performance on television at age of 10.

Dolly Parton in 1977 Image: AP Photo/picture alliance

2. No 'Dumb Blonde'

Multiple sources have reported Parton's IQ to be at least 140. Her first song, which entered the US country charts on January 21, 1967, was "Dumb Blonde." In it, she sings "this dumb blonde ain't nobody's fool." It was a bold start for her entry into 1960s show business, at the time dominated by men.

"I'm not offended by all the dumb blonde jokes because I know I'm not dumb… and I also know that I'm not blonde," she said of the stereotype.

3. Impressive parade of wigs

Across her seven-decade career, Parton loved following fashion trends — especially when it comes to hairstyles.

Her trademark platinum blonde hair, though — as mentioned above — was never truly her own. Rather than spoil her hair with bleaching, she began wearing wigs from early on. It's said her collection numbered over 350 different wigs.

Even wigs need styling: Parton, who appeared in the film 'Steel Magnolias,' visited the Broadway show in 1988 Image: Mark Lenihan/AP Photo/picture alliance

Parton never made a secret of her cosmetic surgeries. Over time, she used it to change her face and figure — but she always remained the friendly superstar with a big heart.

In 2025, Forbes magazine valued Parton's fortune at around $450 million (€387 million). She shared her wealth with people in need for decades — in particular in her home state of Tennessee, but also around the globe.

4. Promoting reading for kids

Since 1995, Parton's The Dollywood Foundation has been sponsoring books for children as part of her Imagination Library program. From the day a child is born, parents can apply to receive a book every month up until the age of 5. More than 300 million books have already been distributed in five English-speaking countries: the US, Canada, Australia, UK and Ireland.

Dolly Parton donated her royalties to good causes Image: Mark Humphrey/AP Photo/picture alliance

The program is funded by the foundation itself, government support and private donors. Recently, however, some Republican-governed states in the US have announced plans to scrap financial support for the Imagination Library. Parton, who didn't have children of her own, founded the library program in honor of her father Robert Lee Parton — who was unable to read.

Each year, the foundation also awards five university scholarships to high school graduates from Sevier County. The Dolly Parton Scholarships of $15,000 are aimed at "students who have a dream they wish to pursue and who can successfully communicate their plan and commitment to realize their dreams," as stated on the foundation's website.

5. A million dollars during COVID

In 2020, Parton donated $1 million to the Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, where the biotechnology company Moderna was working on a COVID-19 vaccine.

On the BBC's "The One Show" in November 2020, she said of her donation: "I'm a very proud girl today to know I had anything at all to do with something that's going to help us through this crazy pandemic."

A few months later, she received the vaccine on camera and rewrote her hit-song "Jolene" to "Vaccine" for the occasion.

6. Hundreds of 'Jolene' covers

"Jolene" is one of the most frequently covered songs in pop music history. The web portal cover.info notes over 80 official cover versions — from famous artists to indie musicians. Countless other versions can be heard on YouTube and other platforms.

One of the most popular covers was the raw and gritty 2004 interpretation by US duo The White Stripes. Parton herself has recorded several versions of her famous hit — accompanied by a cappella group Pentatonix, for instance, or alongside her famous godchild, pop star Miley Cyrus. In 2016, all of them got together to perform it live together on The Voice.

7. Two world hits in one day

Parton wrote both "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You" on the same day in 1972. When Whitney Houston covered the latter two decades later, it became an instant global hit.

You might be surprised to know that "I Will Always Love You" was never meant to be a romantic song. In fact, it was about Parton ending her professional collaboration with her mentor, country star Porter Wagoner.

Speaking with radio host Howard Stern in 2023, Parton recalled the conflicted emotions she felt when writing the song.

"How am I going to make him understand how much I appreciate everything, but that I have to go? I thought, well, what do you do best? You write songs. So I sat down and I wrote this song."

Dolly Parton at an event to celebrate the expansion of the Imagination Library of Kentucky in 2024 Image: Timothy D. Easley/AP Photo/picture alliance

Houston's '90s cover version earned Parton another $10 million in royalties. Speaking in 2021 on "Watch What Happens Live," she revealed that she invested the money into an office complex in a Black neighborhood in Nashville, Tennessee.

"I just thought, 'This was great. I'm going to be down here with her people, who are my people as well… I think, 'This is the house that Whitney built,'" she said.

8. Not the best doppelganger

Last but not least: Parton said that she once took part in a Dolly Parton drag queen lookalike contest — and lost.

On "The Ellen DeGeneres Show," Parton revealed that she had overdone her styling to avoid being recognized: She made her beauty mark bigger, her breasts larger and her hair bigger. All the contestants had to walk across the stage at a gay bar, and whoever received the most applause was declared the winner. In the end, it wasn't Parton who won.

This article was originally written in German. It was first published on January 18, 2026 and was updated upon news of her death on August 25, 2026.

World.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
World.content:
Representatives of the country music legend told US media that Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer." Parton's career spans more than half a century and includes a wide array of smash hits.

US country music singer Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80.

Her nephew Brian Seaver announced the news in a video posted to Parton's Instagram page.

"After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones," Parton's team later said in a statement to CBS News.

Earlier in the year, Parton canceled a series of shows in Las Vegas citing ongoing treatment for health problems. Late last year, she had rebuffed rumors about her health with typical good humor, declaring in a short video, "I ain't dead yet!"

The 80-year-old singer spent almost all of her life making music and is known all over the world for a series of major hits like "Jolene," "9 to 5" and "I Will Always Love You." Her decades-long career earned her 10 Grammys and 13 Academy of Country Music (ACM) awards.

Country music icon Dolly Parton dies To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What did Parton's nephew say announcing her passing?

Parton's nephew and longstanding head of security Seaver said it was an "honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness," to issue this announcement on her behalf, saying she had asked him to do so long ago.

He hailed her influence both on his life and his family's but also on the wider world's.

"By her example, we believed anything was possible," he said of Parton. "She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history."

"My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly Parton, but so have you," he said. "She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family whether you liked it or not."

Trump pays tribute, says flags will fly at half-staff for a week

US President Donald Trump said he had called for flags around the country to be "lowered" for one week starting on Tuesday night in memory of Parton.

"Rest in Peace, Dolly!" Trump wrote on social media, describing her as "one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER."

"This is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will," he wrote of a fellow famous member of the class of 1946.

Democratic Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer wrote simply: "Rest in peace, Dolly Parton -- a true legend and force for good. May her memory be a blessing."

Dolly Parton: musical tributes

The Academy of Country Music hailed Parton's "unmistakable voice, unforgettable songs, generosity and larger-than-life spirit," saying: "Her music will live on, carrying her voice and her story forward for generations to come."

Beatle Paul McCartney said Parton's "songwriting, her singing and her philanthropy were unrivaled in the world of country music" and said it is "hard to imagine living in a world without Dolly."

"There was no greater honour for me than to have her sing my song 'Let It Be' and, even though I only made a small contribution to it, I am so honored that she did it. I am so proud to have known her and admire her unique talents."

Mick Jagger of The Rolling Stones said: "What a wonderful songwriter and singer Dolly was. She brought so many people together, we will all miss her so much."

"It's hard for me to imagine the world without Dolly," said singer-songwriter Cyndi Lauper. "Dolly's heart was as big as her talent. She used her art, her fame and her money to help so many people. She was a great role model for all of us."

Who was Dolly Parton?

Dolly Rebecca Parton was born on January 19, 1946 in Sevierville into what she called a "dirt poor" Tennessee family in the US south.

She was the fourth of 12 children, growing up in the family's small shack in the Great Smoky Mountains.

From singing her first songs to chickens, Parton graduated to performing in a church, where her grandfather was a preacher.

Her debut album, appropriately titled "Hello, I'm Dolly," was released in 1967 with Parton having barely entered her 20s.

She was prolific in her output. By 1974, Parton was already releasing her 13th studio album. Entitled "Jolene," it included what would become two of Parton's most famous songs, the eponymous first track and the opening track of side two, "I Will Always Love You."

She released a staggering 49 solo studio albums in a career spanning well over half a century, concluding in 2023 with "Rockstar."

Parton was known not only for her voice, stage presence, provocative costumes and ample bust, but also as a rapier wit and a stellar storyteller on stage when she had the mic in her hand between her songs.

Sometimes this would also spill over into her creative process. On a visit to the 2014 Glastonbury music festival in the UK, performing in front of an estimated 180,000 sodden fans braving horrendous weather, she said she had composed a special rap just for them earlier that morning, called "Mud."

Catchier lines included rhymes like "Up to our bums in all this crud," while the crowd soon caught on to the chorus by the second go around — chanting "mud, mud, mud!" on her behalf.

You can read more about the iconic country music legend here: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon

Edited by: Rana Taha

World.title: Grain exports stall as Ukraine steps up attacks on Russia's Black Sea ports
World.content:
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian infrastructure on the Black Sea are disrupting grain and oil exports from the port of Novorossiysk and other key hubs.

When Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke in 2014 about Russia's motives for annexing the Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea, and thus violating international law, he justified it by saying: "We could not allow NATO forces to eventually come to the land of Crimea and Sevastopol, the land of Russian military glory, and cardinally change the balance of forces in the Black Sea area."

What now? Intensified Ukrainian attacks on Novorossiysk, Russia's largest commercial Black Sea port, have caused significant disruptions to oil and grain shipments in recent weeks. The Russian navy no longer dominates the region. And exporting goods via the Black Sea is becoming increasingly difficult for Russia because of Ukraine's drone strikes. It is only possible to reorganize logistics partially.

If the attacks continue at such intensity, the consequences for Russian exporters and the national budget could be significant, experts told DW.

Container ships and other vessels have also come under attack Image: Igor Onuchin/TASS/ZUMA/picture alliance

Novorossiysk major Russian hub for exports

Novorossiysk has been a major hub for Russian exports since the 19th century and even today it remains Russia's largest port in terms of cargo volume, as well as one of the largest in Europe. Up to a third of Russia's grain exports are handled through the hub, which is located close to the country's major agricultural regions. Crude oil, metals and containerized goods also pass through the port.

Recent Ukrainian maritime and aerial drone attacks have severely disrupted shipments, particularly of grain. Andrei Sisov, the head of SovEcon, a research and consulting firm specialized in agriculture, uses Telegram to follow the developments. On August 12, he posted that the Novorossiysk Bread Products Plant (NKHP ) — one of Russia's largest grain export terminals — and the Novorossiysk grain terminal had ceased operations. A day later, KSK, one of Russia's largest deep-water grain terminals, also halted its operations. Operations at a major grain terminal in Taman had already come to a standstill at the end of July. Prior to that, Ukraine paralyzed operations at the shallow-water ports of the Sea of Azov.

At the time of publication, only Tuapse, the smallest of Russia's deep-water grain terminals, was still in operation. "This means that virtually all Russian grain exports via the Azov-Black Sea basin are blocked," Sisov said.

Ukrainian drone attacks are doing consistent damage to Russian infrastructure Image: Vantor/Handout/REUTERS

Oil exports also affected

The situation regarding oil exports is not quite as dramatic but while they have not come to a complete standstill, they are frequently disrupted. According to the British news agency Reuters, the Sheskharis terminal — Russia's main oil export facility on the Black Sea, handling some 700,000 barrels of crude oil per day — halted loadings on August 14, which resumed only two days later.

According to London-based Argus Media, a global energy and commodity price reporting agency, Russia could have 45 million metric tons of wheat — Russia's main agricultural export good — for export in 2026 to 2027. However, the situation in the Black Sea, through which about 90% of shipments are usually routed, will make it almost impossible to supply the global market.

Sisov of SovEcon estimated that "many Russian producers will not survive this season, especially after several years of deteriorating financial conditions."

Because exports have come to a standstill, surplus grain will have to be sold on the domestic market, which is already putting downward pressure on prices. Even if exports were to recover over time, there will still be problems. August is usually when shipments peak and it will be difficult to deliver anything no sent this month because terminals tend to operate at full capacity during the autumn anyway.

Ukraine's desperate search for farm labor To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Ukrainian grain exports also decrease

The escalation of hostilities in the Azov and Black Sea regions will also be felt on the global market since Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter.

Ukrainian grain exports have also fallen sharply since there are attacks on both sides. In the past month, Russia too has stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian ports and ships that are docked there.

"The disruptions have blocked out good wheat harvests in Ukraine and Russia from accessing global market," Xiaoyi Deng from Argus Media told DW. "Both have struggled to work with alternative infrastructure, such as Baltic ports (via rail) or Danube River ports but the alternatives would not be up for full replacement."

According to the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Helsinki-based think tank, the port of Novorossiysk "loaded 30% less oil than during the same period last year" in the first two weeks of August. The decline was preceded by a Ukrainian strike on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) marine terminal on July 19.

How Ukraine fights in the Black Sea without a navy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Isaac Levi, an energy analyst at CREA, pointed out that damage to infrastructure was not the only reason for shipments to fall. He said that "strikes on vessels have discouraged ships from calling at ports considered major targets." According to US business news channel Bloomberg, a Greek tanker believed to be carrying Russian oil came under attack on August 17.

"If these constraints persist through August, Russia will find it increasingly difficult to simply defer shipments and make up the lost volumes later," Levi said. "Russia can reroute barrels, but it cannot reroute infrastructure. The most plausible alternatives include the Baltic ports of Primorsk and Ust-Luga.

"But rerouting oil through the Baltic Sea ports would significantly increase transportation times and costs compared with Black Sea exports, while available capacity remains too small to replace significant volumes from Novorossiysk."

This article was originally published in Russian.

World.title: El encargo del Gobierno de Ayuso a la inmobiliaria de lujo que vendió el ático: “Entre 250 y 400 metros y una gran terraza”
World.content:
La Comunidad de Madrid valoró comprar una vivienda de cuatro millones en el paseo del Pintor Rosales antes de decantarse por el apartamento de Chamberí

Las instrucciones eran claras: se buscaba ático de lujo por Chamberí o alrededores. Entre enero y marzo, un mes antes de la adquisición por parte de la empresa pública Planifica Madrid del polémico ático, el Gobierno de Isabel Díaz Ayuso ya buscaba pisos que tuvieran, de entrada, las siguientes características: “Entre 250 y 400 metros cuadrados y una gran terraza”. Así lo han confirmado a EL PAÍS fuentes cercanas a la operación. Son detalles muy parecidos a los del ático que la empresa pública terminó comprando finalmente por 6,3 millones y que cuenta con 485 metros cuadrados y casi 200 metros de terraza. Este se anunciaba en las redes sociales de la inmobiliaria desde el 31 de enero por 6,6 y, antes incluso, en su portfolio. En ese momento fue cuando un alto cargo de Planifica Madrid contactó con la exclusiva inmobiliaria de lujo afincada en La Moraleja a través de un anuncio en internet, detallan estas mismas fuentes. La agencia les mostró al menos dos propiedades.

La primera, ubicada en la zona de Argüelles, concretamente en el paseo del Pintor Rosales, contaba con unos 350 metros cuadrados, con una terraza de 200. Su precio era de cuatro millones de euros. No convenció. A la segunda fue la vencida: el ya célebre ático de la empresaria Astrid Gil-Casares. De estas dos, la opción más cara. “El proceso se prolongó durante aproximadamente un mes y medio antes de la firma de la escritura”, aseguran estas mismas fuentes, justo para que hubiera una negociación por el precio y llegar a un acuerdo. Por su parte, Planifica Madrid, al ser preguntada por esta cuestión, se limita a responder que se remite a las explicaciones que ya se han dado.

La Consejería de Presidencia, de quien depende Planifica Madrid, no ha explicado quién dio la orden a la empresa pública de buscar un piso con esas características precisamente en la zona de Chamberí, donde ha crecido y vivido siempre Ayuso, o el barrio vecino, a escasos minutos a pie de las calles en las que ha pasado toda su vida. Tampoco por qué la compañía optó por buscar dicho apartamento en una inmobiliaria de lujo de La Moraleja, que no se dedica a la venta de oficinas, sino a la venta de viviendas exclusivas, entre ellas el citado ático.

Después de que este periódico desvelara la operación, el Gobierno regional lo puso a la venta por 6,69 millones de euros con el argumento de que el dinero será destinado a paliar los efectos de los incendios que han asolado la zona oeste de la Comunidad de Madrid durante el verano. Esto, sin embargo, es complicado, ya que el dinero obtenido de esa futura venta no podrá destinarse de forma directa ni inmediata a los afectados por los incendios porque el inmueble no pertenece a las arcas de la Comunidad, sino a una sociedad mercantil pública con patrimonio y cuentas propias.

El ático comprado por la Comunidad de Madrid. JUAN BARBOSA

El montante final, de venderse, se quedará dentro de Planifica Madrid tras la operación, por lo que la única vía legal para transferirlo al Gobierno regional pasa por una operación societaria como reparto de dividendo o reducción de capital. El inmueble se ha sacado al mercado por casi 400.000 euros más de lo que costó.

En todo caso, la Comunidad de Madrid pretende dar carpetazo al asunto tras semanas de bandazos: “Chao, pescao”, llegó a decir este lunes la presidenta. La hipotética venta, sin embargo, no disipa ninguna de las dudas que plantea la compra. Entre ellas, ¿para qué podía querer el Gobierno de Ayuso un ático de lujo con uso residencial que queda en pleno barrio de Chamberí, donde creció la presidenta, y que está justo enfrente de donde vive la madre de Ayuso?

Desde el Gobierno regional aludieron a que el inmueble serviría de “oficina” mientras se llevaban a cabo unas obras en la Puerta del Sol, pero el piso no puede tener uso exclusivo de oficina.

Este martes, la Consejería de Presidencia, de quien depende Planifica Madrid, no ha respondido a la pregunta de quién dio la orden de buscar un inmueble con estas características y en esa zona de Madrid. Las incógnitas se acumulan y las explicaciones se antojan escasas incluso en el seno del propio PP. Fuentes cercanas a la compra subrayan que cuando se dieron estas especificaciones de búsqueda, en ningún momento se precisó que debía ser un inmueble que pudiera albergar oficinas o despachos.

Promora, la inmobiliaria que cerró la venta, es una empresa especializada desde hace casi 50 años en viviendas de lujo. Su catálogo está compuesto por chalés, adosados, pisos, áticos y parcelas en algunas de las zonas más cotizadas de Madrid, como La Moraleja, La Finca, Somosaguas, El Viso, el barrio de Salamanca, Chamberí o Almagro. En ningún caso vende oficinas, y la normativa municipal prohíbe que estas se puedan crear en las plantas donde están ubicados los inmuebles que solicitó visitar el Gobierno regional al comienzo de este año. Este lunes, Ayuso volvió a insistir en ello haciendo alusión al polémico ático: “Es un inmueble destinado a oficinas que además puede albergar despachos, por cierto, como tienen en otras plantas”.

Tal y como reveló eldiario.es, Ayuso llevaba ya tiempo buscando piso en Chamberí. Lo hizo primero con la ayuda de su jefe de despacho en la Presidencia de la Comunidad de Madrid, Álvaro Sanz. Este, según contó este medio, contactó con una propiedad, organizó las visitas y participó en la negociación del precio. Ese primer inmueble por el que se interesó Ayuso tenía unos 100 metros cuadrados y estaba anunciado por 850.000 euros. Acompañada de sus escoltas, la presidenta lo visitó por primera vez el 1 de diciembre. Tras un segundo vistazo junto a su pareja, Alberto González Amador, finalmente la compra no se llevó a término.

Una de las estancias del inmueble del Paseo del General Martínez Campos. Interior de la vivienda comprada por la empresa pública Planifica Madrid. Terraza del ático del Paseo del General Martínez Campos. Vista del interior de la vivienda comprada por la Comunidad de Madrid.

La información revelada por eldiario.es llegó a la Asamblea el 16 de abril, justo dos días después de que se firmara la compra del ático del paseo del General Martínez Campos. La portavoz de Más Madrid, Manuela Bergerot, reprochó a Ayuso que hubiera utilizado a un miembro de su gabinete para negociar la adquisición de un piso particular. La presidenta se había negado minutos antes a responder a su pregunta sobre el plan de su Gobierno para los próximos meses. “La vida le trata bien, presidenta”, comenzó Bergerot. “Ahora su jefe de despacho se pone el traje de Tecnocasa para conseguirle su tercer pisito”, añadió. Ayuso respondió que no ofrecería ningún detalle sobre su plan de Gobierno mientras no dejaran de “insultarla”.

Por ahora, se desconoce si Planifica Madrid examinó otras propiedades a través de agencias diferentes y si Ayuso acudió a ver estas viviendas. No obstante, la inmobiliaria niega que la persona que realizó las visitas del piso del paseo Pintor Rosales y el ático de General Martínez Campos fuera el propio Sanz. La búsqueda de una vivienda de lujo con una gran terraza añade nuevas incógnitas en la explicación del Gobierno regional de que un ático que, en teoría, se compró como recurso temporal mientras duraban unas obras. “Se trata de un inmueble que fue adquirido para ponerlo al servicio de las necesidades que pudieran tener las distintas consejerías y como apoyo a las sedes institucionales de la Comunidad de Madrid”, ha indicado este martes el consejero de Presidencia, el hombre señalado por Ayuso y por Alberto Núñez Feijóo para dar explicaciones sobre la vivienda, Ángel García Martín. Este comparecerá pronto ante el pleno de la Asamblea regional para explicar la polémica, pero por ahora su versión tampoco encaja con la búsqueda de una vivienda grande y con terraza.

Tampoco está claro por qué se recurrió a Planifica Madrid, una empresa que “compra y vende inmuebles a lo largo de todo el año”, según defendió Ayuso en más de una ocasión desde que EL PAÍS reveló la compra del ático. Esa también es una verdad a medias. La empresa vende suelo o parcelas ―en general para uso residencial protegido, comercial, industrial o dotacional―, gestiona obras públicas de todo tipo en los municipios de la región, alquila algunos de los edificios en propiedad a la Administración o lleva a cabo encargos de las consejerías, como la rehabilitación de la plaza de toros de Ventas, por ejemplo, pero la compraventa de inmuebles para oficinas de la Comunidad de Madrid no entra, ni mucho menos, entre sus atribuciones habituales.

De hecho, en los últimos cinco años, solo ha adquirido dos inmuebles: las oficinas de su sede, por casi siete millones de euros en 2022; y el año pasado la antigua casa del poeta Vicente Aleixandre, conocida como Velintonia, por algo más de tres millones, que será la próxima Casa de la Poesía. En 2025 también se hizo con el terreno protegido de 408 hectáreas de la finca de El Garzo, en Las Rozas, por unos cinco millones. Estas dos últimas compras se incluyen como adquisiciones recientes en los presupuestos de 2026. Para llevarlas a cabo, se aprobó una modificación presupuestaria. Nada de esto ha ocurrido con la compra de un ático que, ahora se sabe, fue objeto de deseo meses antes de su adquisición.

World.title: Por la Comarca de la Sidra de Asturias entre historia, naturaleza, pueblos y cultura
World.content:
Una de las calles de la localidad asturiana de Villaviciosa, uno de los municipios que forman parte de la Comarca de la Sidra.

El Principado es un paraíso natural, gastronómico y artístico cada día más apreciado como privilegiado destino turístico. Y la sidra, la bebida más popular y su símbolo identitario más universal

Emprendemos un viaje por la Comarca de la Sidra de Asturias, para, entre culín y culín, descubrir algunos de los grandes atractivos de esta emblemática tierra y todos los secretos de esta bebida milenaria. La comarca o mancomunidad sidrera asturiana es un territorio al que dan vida seis municipios del centro-oriente asturiano: Colunga, Nava, Cabranes, Villaviciosa, Bimenes y Sariegu. Tomaremos como punto de partida Nava, población popularmente conocida como “El Corazón de la Sidra”, y que cuenta con un interesante e interactivo Museo de la Sidra, así como con el Festival de la Sidra, declarado de Interés Turístico Nacional y que cada año se celebra la segunda semana de julio.

Para aprovechar el tiempo, lo ideal es visitar el museo a primera hora (durante su horario de verano, hasta el 15 de octubre, abre a las 11.00; lunes cerrado). De esta forma, encontraremos poca gente y la visita será más agradable. En el museo tendremos ocasión de conocer el origen e historia de la sidra, así como el proceso que debe tener lugar antes de poder disfrutar de esta chispeante bebida. También conoceremos cómo se elaboran las distintas variedades —natural, espumosa, filtrada, y de hielo—, el porqué y el cómo hay que escanciar la sidra. Todo ello ilustrado con amenas explicaciones, vídeos, herramientas, prensas o llagares, envasadoras… Después de la visita y de conocer lo laborioso que resulta hacerla, entenderemos la mucha razón que tiene Luis Benito, director de la Cátedra Universitaria de la Sidra de Asturias, al afirmar: “La sidra es un producto de lujo, a precios populares”. Benito fue, además, la persona que más contribuyó a que la Unesco proclamase en 2024 patrimonio cultural inmaterial de la humanidad a la sidra asturiana.

Más información Las mejores terrazas de los cafés históricos de Viena

En cuanto al origen de la sidra, pese a que existen registros históricos que hablan de que los egipcios ya fermentaban manzanas, y que griegos y romanos disponían de una bebida parecida a la sidra, es a través del geógrafo griego Estrabón —siglo I a.C.—y del historiador romano Plinio el Viejo —siglo I— cuando tenemos noticia de que, en los pueblos del norte de la Península, existía una bebida elaborada a partir de las manzanas. Pero no es hasta el siglo XVI cuando hay evidencia escrita de que ya se producían en Asturias 35.000 litros de sidra. No obstante, es posible que un primer acontecimiento decisivo en el auge y difusión de la bebida fuera la creación en el siglo IX, por parte del rey Alfonso II, del Primitivo Camino de Santiago, que partía desde Oviedo y que fue la primera ruta de peregrinación de la historia. A partir de entonces, aunque con algún altibajo histórico, el consumo de la sidra no dejó de crecer y apreciarse. Por eso, y porque la sidra asturiana terminó por viajar a los confines del mundo con la gran emigración del pueblo asturiano, podría afirmarse que el viaje y la sidra han ido siempre de la mano.

Villa Maximina, una de las casas indianas que se pueden ver en la localidad asturiana de Nava. Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Después de la sidra y la fabada, lo mejor es una excursión

Lo que se impone después de visitar el Museo de la Sidra es dar una vuelta por Nava y su casco histórico, y quizás acercarse a conocer la pintoresca villa rural de Ceceda, que conserva viejos hórreos y paneras; algunas casas indianas de estilo colonial y una pequeña capilla con frescos. Tampoco hay que dejar de ver en la cercana pedanía de Fuensanta el palacio de La Ferrería; una imponente casa fuerte medieval del siglo XIV, declarada Monumento Histórico Artístico, donde vivió Doña Jimena —mujer de El Cid—. Como todo está muy próximo, probablemente dé tiempo de regresar a Nava para tomarse un vermut en el bar de La Naveta y comer en alguna de sus muchas sidrerías, por ejemplo, en La Plaza.

Vista aérea del palacio de La Ferrería, en la pedanía de Fuensanta. GETTY IMAGES

Como en los meses de verano el día cunde mucho, después de comer, y para bajar los fabes, el pixín y la sidrina, podemos aprovechar y practicar senderismo haciendo alguna ruta que recorra cualquiera de los imponentes entornos naturales de la zona. Las opciones son numerosas. Se puede hacer la ruta de las Foces del Río Pendón (PR-AS 45); un recorrido circular que se inicia al lado de un antiguo balneario y se adentra en un espectacular desfiladero flanqueado por densas masas de hayas y castaños. Es de dificultad media-baja, de algo más de ocho kilómetros, y se realiza más o menos en tres horas. Otra alternativa, aunque más retirada —ya en el concejo de Bimenes—, es la Senda de Los Molinos (PR-AS 141), también circular y de dificultad moderada, que discurre a la vera del río Pra, recorriendo un valle exuberantemente verde, entre castaños, arces, alisos… y cinco antiguos molinos que crean estampas imborrables. La distancia de esta excursión es de poco más de seis kilómetros y su duración aproximada de tres o cuatro horas.

Un senderista por la Senda de Los Molinos. WHPics / Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Si lo de andar no te apasiona, puedes sustituir el senderismo por acercarte a conocer Santa María de Narzana —en el concejo de Sariego—, una interesante iglesia románica del siglo XII, que conserva portada y ábsides decorados con curiosos motivos zooantropomórficos.

Un pueblo encantador y un conocido ‘llagar’

Partiendo de Nava en dirección a Villaviciosa, un lugar de obligada parada es el pueblo de Torazu, perteneciente al concejo de Cabranes. Se localiza en un pequeño altiplano desde el que se tienen unas privilegiadas vistas del campo y las montañas astures. Reconocido como uno de Los Pueblos más Bonitos de España y distinguido con Premio Príncipe de Asturias al Pueblo Ejemplar en 2008, es un destacado ejemplo de la arquitectura popular asturiana. Conserva numerosos hórreos, la capilla porticada de Nuestra Señora de la Sienra y la iglesia de San Martín el Real; un templo barroco del siglo XVII, situado en la parte más elevada de esta pequeña y coqueta localidad de no más de 100 habitantes. Dispone también de un estupendo establecimiento para alojarse; se trata de La Hostería de Torazo, un lugar con spa y piscina acristalada con inmejorables vistas al más genuino paisaje interior asturiano.

Después de hacer noche en Torazu y volviendo al hilo conductor de este viaje, resulta obligado visitar un llagar (en castellano lagar), que no es otra cosa que la prensa con la que se extrae el mosto de la manzana y, por extensión, también el nombre que recibe el lugar, o bodega, en la que se elabora la sidra. Una buena opción puede ser acercarse al llagar e instalaciones de Viuda de Angelón, casa fundada en 1947 y uno de los 34 únicos llagares que trabaja en el Principado según los estrictos criterios del Consejo Regulador de la Denominación de Origen Protegida, que establece que en la elaboración de la sidra solo se pueden utilizar 76 variedades de manzana, de las más de 550 que se cultivan en Asturias.

Según la época en que se vaya, se podrán presenciar todas las fases del proceso de elaboración de la sidra. Nos explicarán las dos fermentaciones que tiene que experimentar el mosto de la manzana para convertirse en sidra natural: la alcohólica, para transformar los azúcares en alcohol y gas carbónico; y la maloláctica para convertir el acido málico, en láctico y así suavizar la acidez de la bebida. También nos hablarán de lo que dura el proceso en los toneles —de una a tres semanas la primera fermentación, y de tres a cinco meses la segunda—. Te ilustrarán también sobre los tipos de sidra existentes. O te contarán que, al principio, la sidra se servía directamente desde el barril, a través de la espicha (un pequeño grifo que hace salir a presión la sidra del tonel), hasta que hace 150 años empezó a embotellarse y a escanciarse, para así liberar el gas carbónico y resaltar los aromas de la sidra.

Del románico más genuino a los pueblos más bellos del Cantábrico

La siguiente etapa del viaje se centra en recorrer la que probablemente sea la mayor concentración de templos prerrománicos y románicos de Asturias y una de las mayores densidades de arquitectura medieval de toda Europa. La lista es casi inabarcable. Entre las iglesias más destacadas están San Salvador de Priesca, iglesia originaria del siglo X y monumento nacional desde 1913; Santa María de Llugás, un conjunto de singular belleza, que, después de Covadonga, es el principal santuario mariano de Asturias y Bien de Interés Cultural desde 1994; y San Juan de Amandi, reconocida construcción románica con un esbelto ábside semicircular y una fantástica colección de capiteles, reconocida como monumento nacional desde 1931. Bien de Interés Cultural, igualmente, es San Julián de Viñón, iglesia construida en el siglo XII y uno de los mejores ejemplos de románico rural de la zona, que, además, está muy cerca del Museo de la Escuela Rural de Asturias que también merece una visita; ambos en el concejo de Cabranes.

La iglesia de Santa María de la Oliva, en Villaviciosa. Aliaksandr Mazurkevich ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Pero si tuviéramos que resaltar un ejemplo especialmente sobresaliente de arte prerrománico y románico asturiano de la zona, ese, sin duda, sería el conjunto de Valdediós, con la iglesia y el monasterio de Santa María (fundado en 1200 y declarado Monumento Nacional en 1931), y, sobre todo, la iglesia de San Salvador, uno de los más hermosos monumentos del Principado y obra cumbre de la última etapa del arte prerrománico; conocido como el Conventín. Esta iglesia de tres naves fue consagrada en el año 893 y tiene notables influencias mozárabes, tanto en su estructura como en sus pinturas, además se encuentra situada en un paraje lleno de encanto y serenidad.

La iglesia de San Salvador de Valdediós, conocida popularmente como el Conventín. Alexei Fateev ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Pese a abarcar un espacio muy limitado, este formidable circuito de arte prerrománico y románico de la Comarca de la Sidra es prácticamente imposible de visitarse en un solo día. Como en algún momento habrá que comer y pensar en alojarse en algún sitio, una buena idea podría ser hacerlo en Narbasu, un hotel y restaurante que la familia Manzano ha montado en el antiguo palacio de Rubianes; una histórica construcción iniciada en el siglo XIV, enclavada en un paraje privilegiado en las inmediaciones de un río y con las montañas asturianas como imponente telón de fondo. La filosofía del lugar es integrarse y ser respetuoso con su entorno, haciendo, por ejemplo, que los productos vegetales utilizados sean de sus propios huertos y el resto, de pequeños productores de las inmediaciones. El lugar respira sosiego y hospitalidad y el restaurante tiene toda la calidad de una carta de cocina tradicional inspirada y avalada técnicamente por Nacho Manzano, reconocido chef —tres estrellas Michelin—, de Casa Marcial. Si comes allí, y lo pides, te maridarán la comida con los diferentes tipos de sidra.

Continuando con nuestro periplo turístico y sidrero, nos encaminamos hacia el litoral; la Comarca de la Sidra ofrece kilómetros de una costa con multitud de espléndidas playas y acantilados que disfrutar, así como algunos de los pueblos más bonitos de Asturias y de la cornisa cantábrica. Pero antes de llegar al mar, si tenemos tiempo, podemos desviarnos a Sietes para ver uno de los conjuntos de hórreos y paneras mejor conservados de todo el Principado. También podemos hacer un alto en Gobientes para conocer la iglesia románica de Santiago —Monumento Histórico-Artístico—, cuya construcción se remonta al siglo X y desde la que parte una pequeña senda, de un par de kilómetros, hacia la cascada de Obaya; un paraje natural que también merece la pena conocer.

Una calle de Sietes, donde espera uno los conjuntos de hórreos y paneras mejor conservados de todo el Principado. FedevPhoto ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Ya oliendo la sal, veremos las populosas playas de Isla —con sus llamativos bosques de eucaliptos— y, especialmente, la preciosa playa de Rodiles, en Villaviciosa, rodeada de vegetación y famosa entre los surfistas por tener un singular tipo de ola. La otra playa que no puede dejar de disfrutarse es la de La Griega, en Colunga, magnífico arenal en el que desemboca el río Libardón. Cerca de su extremo derecho se pueden ver imponentes ignitas (huellas fosilizadas) de dinosaurios, descubiertas en los años noventa. Hablando de dinosaurios, muy cerca de allí se encuentra el Museo del Jurásico de Asturias, con monumentales reproducciones de estos gigantes del pasado.

Las ignitas (huellas fosilizadas) de dinosaurios junto a la playa de La Griega, en Colunga. Alba Boix ( Alamy /CORDON PRESS )

Antes de abandonar la costa para dirigirnos a Villaviciosa, merecen una parada Lastres y Tazones, ambos reconocidos entre los Pueblos más Bonitos de España. El primero, creciendo escalonada y vistosamente desde el puerto hacia los acantilados que dominan la población, y el segundo, exhibiendo sus coloridas casas de pescadores y sus calles empedradas, y teniendo la singular significación histórica de haber sido la primera tierra española que pisó Carlos V a su llegada a la península Ibérica. En los dos se puede comer bien en cualquiera de sus restaurantes, aunque si se quiere disfrutar de unas vistas espectaculares, el restaurante El Mirador de Lastres regala un impresionante panorama de toda la bahía.

Calle en la localidad asturiana de Lastres. Politi Markovina ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Ría, piedras medievales y sidra viajera

La siguiente y prácticamente última etapa es Villaviciosa, conocida como “Capital Manzanera de España”, y famosa tanto por su ría y magnífico casco histórico como por ser la sede de la sidra El Gaitero. El concejo de Villaviciosa tiene el mayor número de pumaradas (plantaciones de manzanos) de Asturias, lo cual hace que su campo sea una explosión de color con la floración de los manzanos en primavera y, a finales del verano o principios de otoño, un espectáculo de árboles cargados de fruta.

La sidrería El Gaitero, en Villaviciosa. Ingenui ( GETTY IMAGES )

Villaviciosa tiene muchas historias que contar y una de las más importantes está relacionada con la sidra, porque fueron las industrias sidreras de la población las que popularizaron en todo el mundo la sidra espumosa o achampañada, que fue creada por el productor gijonés Tomás Zarracina en 1857, como respuesta a la añoranza que sentía la enorme colonia de emigrantes asturianos —más de medio millón— repartida por México, Argentina, Cuba… de poder celebrar sus fiestas con la bebida típica de su tierra; algo que antes resultaba imposible, porque la sidra natural no resistía el viaje y se estropeaba, y que no sucedería después con la sidra sometida al método champenoise (segunda fermentación en botella). La empresa que mejor supo producir y comercializar la sidra espumosa y viajera fue sidra El Gaitero, entre otras cosas, con su popular eslogan publicitario: “Sidra El Gaitero, famosa en el mundo entero”. Esta compañía sigue produciendo en Villaviciosa y organiza visitas guiadas por sus instalaciones, en las que muestran sus antiguos llagares o bodegas, que son como el interior de enormes y hermosas catedrales, al tiempo que explican todo el proceso de elaboración de su producto estrella.

Antes o después de visitar las bodegas hay que dar un paseo por el monumental casco histórico de Villaviciosa, que sorprende con sus numerosas casas blasonadas y con sus iglesias; especialmente Santa María de la Oliva, un templo románico-gótico del siglo XII, con artística portada principal. Otros edificios de gran interés son la iglesia parroquial de San Francisco, construcción del siglo XVII, y la capilla de la Concepción. Además de todo lo dicho, la mayor singularidad de la villa quizá sea que está a la vera de la ría que lleva su nombre y que tiene la consideración de Reserva Natural, por su característico ecosistema marítimo-fluvial y por ser un importante refugio de aves.

Una sugerencia que puede ser del gusto de adultos y, sobre todo, para los más pequeños, es la visita —a la salida de Villaviciosa— de la finca Los Caserinos, una granja ecológica familiar muy conocida en la zona, que elabora productos naturales de gran calidad (quesos, yogures bio, y arroz con leche, helados…) y que para los niños puede resultar un plan perfecto, porque la granja tiene cabras, vacas, ovejas, gallinas, caballos… a los que poder ver y tocar; además de aprender a hacer queso.

Como alguien dijo: “La sidra es una bebida ligera, anima a hablar y compartir, pone de buen humor, es diurética y buena para la salud, alegra el corazón y, por su baja graduación, es una buena compañera de viaje”. Pues eso.

World.title: Italia quiere poner orden en el caos de sus 12.000 playas privadas: más transparencia y nuevas tasas
World.content:
Entre el 33% y el 42% de los arenales del país son de pago. El Gobierno de Meloni, presionado por Bruselas, abrirá a concurso su gestión

Italia presume de sus 8.000 kilómetros de costa, pero disfrutar de ellos no siempre es gratis. Mientras que en otras partes ir a la playa significa buscar un hueco en la arena, en Italia la experiencia suele ser muy distinta. Encontrar un espacio donde plantar la sombrilla sin pagar puede convertirse en toda una aventura. En amplios tramos del litoral, el acceso al mar está gestionado por empresas privadas, mediante concesiones públicas, que han transformado las playas en un negocio multimillonario. El resultado es una de las estampas más características del verano italiano: bosques interminables de sombrillas perfectamente alineadas, acompañadas de sus respectivas tumbonas, esperando a ser alquiladas por precios que pueden superar los 35 euros al día.

Este modelo, muy arraigado en el país y marcado por una gestión plagada de irregularidades, afronta una reforma que lleva años aplazándose a pesar de la presión de Bruselas para poner orden. Las playas gestionadas por concesionarios privados no han dejado de ganar terreno. Según la asociación ecologista italiana Legambiente, ocupan ya más del 42% de los arenales del país. El Ministerio de Infraestructuras rebaja esa cifra al 33%, una diferencia que se explica por el criterio utilizado para el cálculo: el Gobierno utiliza para sus cuentas toda la línea costera italiana y no únicamente las zonas aptas para el baño.

Desde hace décadas, las empresas, casi siempre familiares —las concesiones suelen heredarse—, pagan cánones relativamente bajos al Estado por explotar espacios públicos, mientras los precios para los usuarios han aumentado de forma exponencial. Las concesionarias gestionan los servicios como los baños, las duchas, los vestuarios, los aparcamientos, además del alquiler de sombrillas y tumbonas. También controlan los chiringuitos y cafeterías y se encargan de las labores de salvamento. Mientras que las zonas públicas suelen estar descuidadas, a menudo sucias, y desprovistas de servicios públicos.

Se trata de un asunto sensible que divide a la opinión pública italiana. Para unos, las playas de pago garantizan orden, limpieza y comodidad; para otros, representan la privatización de un bien público que debería ser accesible para todos. La principal crítica al sistema es la enorme diferencia entre lo que pagan las concesionarias por explotar las playas y los beneficios que obtienen. El Estado recauda entre 80 y 100 millones de euros al año por las concesiones, mientras que el sector, marcado por la opacidad, mueve más de 2.000 millones de euros anuales, según distintas estimaciones. El propio Tribunal de Cuentas italiano ha advertido de que los cánones abonados por los empresarios no suelen ser proporcionales a los ingresos que obtienen.

Uno de los aspectos más controvertidos del modelo italiano es que las concesiones se han renovado durante años casi por inercia. Sin concursos abiertos ni una competencia efectiva y sin controles ni transparencia, los mismos operadores han conservado la explotación de amplios tramos del litoral público durante generaciones, consolidando un sistema difícil de encontrar en otros países europeos.

Un paso adelante

Bruselas lleva años reclamando cambios. La Comisión considera que Italia incumple la directiva Bolkestein de 2009, que obliga a garantizar la libre competencia en la adjudicación de este tipo de concesiones, y ha presionado repetidamente a Roma. Tras décadas de aplazamientos y enfrentamientos, el Gobierno de Giorgia Meloni ha abordado la cuestión. La reforma aprobada prevé que para el 30 de septiembre de 2027 salgan a concurso público todas las playas de pago, unas 12.000 repartidas por todo el país. Además, las concesiones tendrán una duración limitada, de entre cinco y 20 años, y habrá compensaciones económicas para los actuales titulares por las inversiones y obras que hayan realizado.

La perspectiva de abrir el mercado ha despertado, sin embargo, inquietud entre muchos empresarios del sector, que temen que los concursos favorezcan la entrada de grandes grupos turísticos o fondos de inversión capaces de desplazar a los negocios familiares que tradicionalmente han dominado las costas italianas.

World.title: Students who leave home rarely move far, CBS finds
World.content:
Most young people in the Netherlands who leave home to study move to a university city in their own region, figures from the national statistics office CBS show.

Nearly 32,000 people aged 17 to 22 moved out to live in a university city in 2025. More than 80% came from a different municipality, but most had not gone far.

Amsterdam and Groningen took in the most, with 5,300 and 5,100 – the only cities to draw more than 5,000. About 30% of those who moved to Amsterdam or Rotterdam had already been living there, and many of the rest came from within 50 kilometres.

Groningen draws students mainly from the three northern provinces, Enschede from the east, and Maastricht, Tilburg and Eindhoven from Noord-Brabant and Limburg. Wageningen is the exception, taking students from across the country.

The figures count only domestic moves and leave out international students.

Around 17% of university students in the Netherlands come from abroad, a share that climbs above 60% in Maastricht.

Fewer young people are leaving home to study than a decade ago, down from an average of 36,000 a year between 2015 and 2021, as more stay put. The number spiked above 50,000 in 2023, the year the basic student grant returned and made moving out more affordable.

Where they go also splits along gender lines. Over the five years to 2025, women made up about two-thirds of new arrivals in Maastricht and Nijmegen, while the three cities with a technical university – Delft, Eindhoven and Enschede – drew more men.

World.title: New Oranje coach Xavi calls Netherlands “university of football”
World.content:
New national head coach Xavi Hernandez said he regarded the Netherlands as the “university of football” as he gave his first press conference in Zeist.

The 46-year-old said it was an “honour” to be appointed by the KNVB as the first foreign coach since Austria’s Ernst Happel led the men’s team to the 1978 World Cup final.

Xavi was the KNVB’s third choice for the job after Pep Guardiola, the former Manchester City coach, opted to take a sabbatical from football and Arne Slot, the former Feyenoord and Liverpool coach, preferred to stay in club football.

He has been given a four-year contract until the end of the next World Cup in 2030, with no conditions tied to the Netherlands’ performance at the European Championships in two years’ time.

Most of Xavi’s playing career was spent at Barcelona, where he won eight La Liga titles, many of them under the tutelage of Guardiola, whose playing style was influenced by Dutch legend Johan Cruyff.

He made his international debut for Spain in a friendly game against the Netherlands in 2000 and 10 years later was one of the pivotal members of the team that won the World Cup in 2010, defeating Oranje in the final.

“My feeling today is that I’m going to the university of football,” Xavi said. “I learned a lot during my career as a player and a coach that I want to give back.

Big family

“I believe a lot in this generation,” he added. “We have a lot of talents, but the important thing for me is to create a team, a group and a big family in order to play well.”

Asked how he felt about being the KNVB’s third choice, ahead of youth team coach Michael Reiziger, Xavi said: “It’s not a bad position after Guardiola and Slot. At least we’re on the podium.”

He added that the Dutch “total football” school was the basis for his own style of football as both a player and a coach.

“To dominate, the game, to take the initiative with the ball, and at the same time our goal is to show to everybody a team with passion, with desire and ambition. That is my philosophy,” he said.

“We are here to compete, we are here to enjoy and we are here to win.”

Senior players

The KNVB’s technical director, Nigel de Jong, said Xavi was identified as a candidate because his footballing philosophy aligned closely with the Dutch team’s ambitions to play “attractive, dominant” football.

The coach said he had not made any decisions about which players he will select, but he had already spoken to current team captain Virgil van Dijk and Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong.

Dutch media have speculated that Van Dijk, 35, and leading scorer Memphis Depay, 32, could be dropped from the squad as part of a clear-out of senior players.

De Jong, who worked with Xavi during the Spaniard’s spell as Barcelona coach from 2021 to 2024, has been struggling with injuries for more than a year and was not fully fit during this year’s World Cup.

The coach also said he had been monitoring AZ Alkmaar’s promising 20-year-old midfielder Kees Smit, who narrowly missed out on the World Cup squad this summer.

Oranje will play their first match under his leadership on September 24, when they take on Germany in the Nations League in Amsterdam. “We haven’t yet decided the [squad] list,” Xavi said. “You will see it in three weeks.”

World.title: Vondelkerk fire investigation ends in mystery, police say
World.content:
How the Vondelkerk in Amsterdam went up in flames on New Year’s Eve is still unknown, police have said, after months of trying and failing to establish a criminal cause for the blaze.

Investigators had looked into whether the fire was started deliberately and whether fireworks were to blame. Local residents were interviewed, video footage examined and tips about possible arson followed up, but none of it produced any evidence, police said.

It could also not be established whether fireworks caused the fire. Much of the forensic evidence was destroyed in the blaze itself, police said, and no traces of fireworks were found. With no leads left to pursue, the investigation has stalled.

Years to rebuild

The monumental church on Vondelstraat, close to the Vondelpark, was largely destroyed in the early hours of January 1, when its tower collapsed and much of the roof was lost. It was designed by Pierre Cuypers, the 19th-century architect behind Amsterdam’s Centraal station and the Rijksmuseum, and completed in 1880.

The building served as a Catholic church until it closed in 1977 and has since been used for concerts, offices and community events, with church services returning in 2017. It has been owned since 1996 by heritage restoration body Stadsherstel Amsterdam.

Several fundraising drives were launched after the fire. Stadsherstel said more than €180,000 had been raised within a week, and other appeals brought in tens of thousands of euros more. Rebuilding the church is expected to take years.

World.title: Dutch foundation plans to build underground hospital in Ukraine
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A Dutch organisation is trying to raise funds to build a reinforced underground hospital in Ukraine so soldiers can be treated nearer the front line.

Protect Ukraine and a Norwegian foundation, HMM Healthcare, say they have already secured €750,000 in donations for the project, which is expected to cost €2.5 million in total.

The 600 m2 hospital will be built 8 m below ground and made entirely of concrete, allowing wounded service personnel to be treated in what is effectively a giant bunker.

The organisers hope to have the building fully equipped and operational by February 2027.

Jaap Scholten, a Dutch writer and co-founder of Protect Ukraine, said: “The fact that we have raised three-quarters of a million euros in such a short time shows that people in the Netherlands have not forgotten Ukraine.

“But we are not there yet. Every donation brings us closer to a hospital and stabilisation point that can save many lives.”

Protect Ukraine has around 100 volunteers who run regular trips to Ukraine to deliver goods such as medicines, pop-up tents and pick-up trucks.

Scholten, who lives in Hungary, told NOS he started the organisation after watching people in his neighbourhood handing out fresh fruit, energy bars and blankets to Ukrainian refugees.

“Arranging supplies for Ukrainians is the most effective thing you can do to help,” he said. “That’s why I started Protect Ukraine.”

World.title: Many Dutch children hide upsetting online posts from parents
World.content:
Half of children in the Netherlands aged 10 to 15 sometimes see posts online that frighten or upset them, but many do not tell their parents out of shame or fear of an angry reaction, a government survey has found.

The finding comes as junior digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts launches a new phase of the government’s Blijf in Beeld (“Stay in the picture”) campaign, which encourages parents to talk to their children about what they encounter online and to agree rules on phone use together.

The survey, commissioned by the economic affairs and climate ministry (EZK), found children in the Netherlands now get their first smartphone at the age of 10 on average. Children most often named Snapchat and TikTok as the places they were most likely to come across something unpleasant.

Talk early

Aerdts said parents should start those conversations while children are young, before the influence of friends grows. “Be curious about what they see, including the nice and funny things,” she said, arguing this makes it easier for children to also raise the frightening or harmful side of social media.

Parents should not judge children for what they do online, she added, and should be open about their own use.

The campaign, developed in part with children’s helpline the Kindertelefoon, comes with a printed card that parents and children fill in together. The ministry said 89.4% of children understood why rules on phone use mattered, and half said they welcomed them.

Waiting for Brussels

Aerdts said platforms were not doing enough to protect children. “The online world is really not yet a safe place for children,” she said, adding that this was why the government wants a minimum age for social media use agreed at European level rather than in national law.

That marks a contrast with France, Spain and Greece, which have moved to set their own age limits. France passed a law last month barring under-15s from social media, though its Constitutional Council then ruled the measure unconstitutional in its current form and the government is redrafting it.

Aerdts has previously said she wants to avoid “a mishmash of rules and regulations that will The European Commission is working on its own proposals: last month researchers advised it to ban social media for children under 13, and commission president Ursula von der Leyen has said she will bring forward a proposal to limit children’s use after the summer.

World.title: Shrinkflation eases but manufacturers turn sneaky, watchdog says
World.content:
Shrinkflation is happening less often than a few years ago, but manufacturers are getting better at hiding it, consumer body the Consumentenbond has found in its latest sweep of Dutch supermarket shelves.

The organisation again found dozens of products whose contents had shrunk without a matching drop in price, and received fewer reports from shoppers than in previous years. But a hard core of producers are now shrinking packs so quietly that customers don’t notice.

The clearest example is Blue Band Vloeibaar, the liquid baking product, which dropped from 750 to 700 millilitres in March 2026 while the bottle and front label stayed exactly the same.

The new volume appears only in small print on the side, and the pack is still described as a “voordeelfles”, or value bottle. The recommended price held at €3.65, so shoppers pay more per millilitre either way.

Shrunk more than once

Some products have now been reduced two or three times over. Andrélon conditioner went from 300 to 250 and then to 200ml; on the last step the price rose from €5.49 to €6.49, a 48% increase per 100ml.

A bag of M&M’s, which held 440 grams in 2020, now contains 363 grams, leaving consumers paying about 10% more per 100 grams.

Manufacturers mostly blamed higher costs for packaging, raw materials, energy and transport. Mars, which makes M&M’s, pointed to recently changed rules it said might bar producers from sharing recommended prices – but, the watchdog said, as far as it could tell no such change had taken place.

Consumentenbond director Sandra Molenaar called on politicians to act. “When there is more in a pack, manufacturers shout it from the rooftops,” she said, “but when the contents shrink, they only adjust it quietly on the back.”

She wants producers required to state a reduction clearly on the pack, or supermarkets made to flag it at the shelf, as is already the law in France.

World.title: Fraudsters using iDeal switch to Wero to snare bank customers
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Fraudsters are sending out phishing mails to Dutch bank customers to try to take advantage of the switch from the iDeal payment system to Wero.

The fake messages typically tell customers they are due a refund as a result of the transition to Wero, the European-based system set up under efforts to make EU businesses less dependent on foreign digital services.

Victims are told to verify their identity by clicking on a link in the e-mail, which takes them to a page where the criminals can steal their login details.

The online fraud hotline Fraudehelpdesk.nl said it was currently receiving 100 queries a day about suspicious messages regarding iDeal, after a surge in activity in the last few months.

A frequently seen mail in recent days says the handover took place on August 24 and puts customers under pressure to claim their refund before the “deadline”.

Danial van Delft, CEO of Currence, the company that operates iDeal and Wero, told the Telegraaf: “This is a big change in the payments ecosystem and gives people with bad intentions space to abuse it.

“We see fraudsters becoming more and more inventive. They are trying to latch on to every hook and news item.”

iDeal said people should ignore suspicious emails and not click on links. “iDeal will never ask you to confirm personal details by email, start a verification process or install software,” the company said.

World.title: Villagers at centre of asylum row urge council to heal divide
World.content:
Residents of a Noord-Brabant village at the centre of a bitter row about plans to accommodate 50 asylum seekers have accused the local council of making the problem worse through its poor communications strategy.

Violent protests were staged in Engelen, on the edge of ’s-Hertogenbosch, after the council announced in April it would be housing a group of teenage boys and girls, all under 18, in a former police station on Beverspijken.

Opponents have staged marches to express their concern about women’s safety, while supporters say they have been subjected to a hate campaign, with swastikas and obscene words spray-painted on their homes.

At a council meeting on Monday night, residents on both sides of the divide appealed to the local mayor, Jack Mikkers, to talk to villagers before the final decision is made next month.

Around 100 people packed into the council chamber in Den Bosch and a side room set up as an overspill location for those who were unable to get into the public gallery.

The council says it has an obligation to accommodate asylum seekers under the so-called “spreading law”, which requires all local authorities to take in a fair share in order to ease overcrowding at the reception centre in Ter Apel, Groningen.

“Spend an evening walking through Engelen, ring people’s doorbells and listen,” said Tamara Govers, who organised one of the marches in May. “Come as a person, not an official, without cameras or press releases.”

Blacklist

Astrid van den Broek, who spoke in support of the plan, called for councillors to stop the threats and intimidation. “My name’s been put on a blacklist,” she said, adding that a man who threatened her when she filmed a group putting up protest signs was at the meeting.

“I’ve told security,” she said. “Don’t talk to me about being concerned about our women’s safety if the shelter goes ahead.”

Other villagers said the municipality had been too slow to respond to the menacing atmosphere in the village. “The shelter has driven a wedge between friendships,” said resident Eva Buijs.

Jack Burg, chair of local campaign group Veilig Engelen, said “better communication” from the council could have prevented the situation escalating.

Burg said the plans did not do enough to address concerns about the impact of the refugee centre on quality of life in the village.

“Conditions and rules have not been worked out,” he said. “We need more than this plan for a suitable accommodation facility. We want clarity, but that’s not what this is.”

Strict conditions

The council has set strict conditions for the centre, including a 10pm curfew and night-time security. Residents will have to move out as soon as they turn 18, most likely to smaller groups in Den Bosch.

The municipality also wants the refugee accommodation agency COA to send equal numbers of girls and boys, but that may be difficult to arrange because five out of six underage asylum seekers are male.

Some residents said they were not against accommodating refugees in the village, but called the empty police station on Beverspijken the “wrong location”.

One group produced data from decibel readings taken from the site that showed levels of 83 decibels had been recorded at night – 18db higher than the level permitted by the local environmental plan.

Others questioned whether the council and the COA could be relied on to stick to their agreeement to make the accommodation centre a temporary facility, pointing out that permits for other locations have been extended at the request of the agency.

Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years. The charges relate to statements last year in which Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, suggested that the gas chambers at Auschwitz, which was the Nazis’ main killing centre during the Holocaust, are “fake”. Komunikat o przedstawieniu posłowi do Parlamentu Europejskiego zarzutów publicznego i wbrew faktom zaprzeczania zbrodniom ludobójstwa popełnionym w niemieckim nazistowskim obozie koncentracyjnym i zagłady KL Auschwitz-Birkenau w Oświęcimiu. https://t.co/nLq3XKnXCK — IPN Kraków (@ipn_krakow) August 25, 2026 On Tuesday morning, Braun was summoned to appear as a suspect at the Kraków branch of the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has the power to prosecute crimes relating to the periods when Poland was under Nazi and communist rule. A group of his followers gathered outside the building to express their support for Braun, who finished fourth in last year’s presidential elections. Since then, his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party has risen to around 9% in polls, making it a potential kingmaker after next year’s parliamentary elections. After meeting with Braun, IPN prosecutor Robert Janicki announced that they had presented Braun with charges for “publicly and contrary to the facts denying the crimes of genocide committed by officers of the Third Reich in the German concentration and extermination camp KL Auschwitz-Birkenau”. The charges relate to two interviews Braun gave in July last year. He declared that “Auschwitz with its gas chambers is unfortunately a fake” and said that claims about the use of gas chambers are part of a “propaganda narrative” supporting a “quasi-religious cult”. In actual fact, gas chambers were used at Auschwitz, which was located in German-occupied Poland, to kill around 900,000 people, the vast majority of them Jews. Janicki noted that Braun’s remarks “clearly contradict common historical knowledge based on documents, witness accounts, perpetrators’ statements and findings from past criminal proceedings”. Far-right leader Grzegorz Braun says the gas chambers at Auschwitz are “fake” and it is a “fact” that Jews have committed ritual murder. Prosecutors have launched an investigation into whether he violated Poland's law against denying Nazi crimes https://t.co/7UUKzH5ndG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2025 When Braun originally made his remarks, they were widely condemned in Poland, which suffered enormously under German occupation during World War Two. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek asked the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, to lift his legal immunity so he could be charged. “For me, it is a scandal that, in a country that suffered such enormous war losses, there is a politician who can deny historical facts that are so painful for Poles,” said Żurek at the time, quoted by the Onet news website. “I won’t let this go. We must bring such people to justice.” In March, the European Parliament approved Żurek’s request, allowing Braun to face charges in relation to his Auschwitz comments, as well as for other alleged crimes. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 On Friday last week, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw charged Braun with those other crimes, including the theft of Ukrainian and EU flags he tore down and vandalism of an LGBT+ exhibition being displayed in parliament. In a separate case, in February this year, Żurek also asked the European Parliament to strip Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes over another incident in which he called the gas chambers at both Auschwitz and Majdanek, another Nazi-German camp in occupied Poland, “fake”. Meanwhile, Braun is already on trial in Poland for four other alleged crimes, including using a fire extinguisher to attack a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony in the Polish parliament in December 2023. The trial of Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun for his attacks on a Hanukkah celebration in parliament and a Holocaust lecture has begun.
